title: EOI Non linear Kicker Power Supply
description:
The Australian Synchrotron (AS) is a world-class research facility operated by the Australian Nuclear Science and Technology Organisation (ANSTO), located in Clayton, Victoria. The facility supports advanced research across a broad range of scientific disciplines and plays a critical role in Australia’s innovation and science infrastructure. Operating continuously on a 24/7 basis, the Synchrotron comprises highly specialised laboratory environments, including beamlines, technical workshops, mechanical services areas, and user accommodation.
The purpose of the EOI is for ANSTO to understand the current market capabilities, experiences and delivery method and compliance for the supply a high current and high voltage pulsed power supply (PPS) for a non-linear injection kicker magnet (NLK) in the storage ring (SR).
buyer: Australian Nuclear Science and Technology Organisation

title: AIC Criminology Research Fund 2026
description:
The Commonwealth as represented by the Australian Institute of Criminology (AIC) is seeking sumissions for the Criminology Research Fund 2026.
The Criminology Research Fund (CRF) program is a competitive program that provides funds to support the conduct of high quality, policy-relevant research projects in the area of crime and criminal justice. The CRF is funded through annual contributions by the Commonwealth, State and Territory Governments.
The CRF program is administered by the AIC on the basis of recommendations from the Criminology Research Advisory Council (Advisory Council). The Advisory Council, which includes representatives from each of the contributing Governments, provides recommendations to the Director of the AIC on research priorities and an assessment of applications made under the annual CRF program. The Advisory Council bases its assessment on the recommendations of an Academic Panel chaired by the Academic Advisor (an AIC research staff member).
The AIC will award contracts in varying values.

vendorPanelDetails.desiredOutcomes:
The purpose of the design is to deliver a functional, safe and compliant public carpark that supports the current and future use of the Park. The carpark solution is required to achieve high quality integration with the surrounding parkland and associated infrastructure. This includes:

- Clear and accessible pedestrian and cyclist connections to existing and proposed park facilities.

- Integration with the park’s spatial structure, circulation network and desire lines.

- Responds to landscape character, landform, vegetation, visual quality and considers place and context. Existing trees and landform are to be retained and integrated.

- Edges and interfaces that transition appropriately.

To achieve these outcomes, the design must adopt a landscape-led approach. The engagement of a suitably qualified landscape architect is critical to resolving the interface between the carpark and the surrounding parkland.

publicQuestions.question:
We have the following queries which would appreciate Council's response:

1) ISO 9001 requirement

The Services state that all services, including subconsultant services, are to be carried out under a QMS certified to AS/NZS ISO 9001, except where the Principal accepts otherwise, whereas the Tender Schedule asks whether the Tenderer has either an ISO 9001-certified system or can demonstrate equivalent systems are in place.

Please confirm that a consultant without third-party ISO 9001 certification may submit a conforming tender where it demonstrates an equivalent documented QMS, project-specific Quality Plan, independent checking and QA records acceptable to Council.

2) Construction budget definition

The Services identify an early construction estimate of approximately $2 million, but state that an indicative construction budget has not yet been determined.

Please confirm whether $2 million is to be treated as a design budget/target, and whether it includes or excludes contamination remediation, Foreshore Road/deceleration lane works, TfNSW works, landscape works, lighting/CCTV, authority charges, preliminaries, contingency and GST.

3) Overall completion milestone

Council anticipates award in late November 2026 and commencement in mid-December 2026. The specified programme includes 12 weeks for concept review/endorsement, 12 weeks for community consultation, two-week reviews at both 50% and 75% detailed design, followed by IFT and IFC.

Please confirm Council's required target dates for endorsed Concept Design, 50% DD, 75% DD, IFT and IFC, and whether the 12-week concept approval and 12-week community consultation periods may overlap.

4) Existing survey information

The Scope refers to available survey, utilities, easements and levels, while the pricing schedule separately nominates a registered surveyor for boundary definition.

Please confirm exactly what existing feature/topographic, cadastral/boundary, easement and level survey information Council will provide, including its format and currency. Is a new registered cadastral/boundary survey required within the base scope?

5) Geotechnical and pavement investigations

Existing 2018 TfNSW investigations include test pits to approximately 1.8–1.9 m depth, with basecourse and underlying marine sand deposits recorded.

Please confirm whether Council considers the existing TfNSW geotechnical information sufficient for detailed pavement design, or whether the Consultant is expected to allow for new geotechnical investigation, pavement cores/test pits, DCP/CBR testing and laboratory testing in the base tender price.

6) Supplementary contamination investigations

The Scope requires the Consultant to identify and undertake additional investigations as necessary, including supplementary contamination investigations, subject to Council approval.

Should the tender lump sum include an allowance for supplementary contamination sampling/testing, or should such investigation be treated as an additional service/provisional allowance once the PSI, DSI and RAP have been reviewed and specific data gaps identified?

7) Environmental/remediation consultant scope

The existing site investigations identify asbestos-containing material and uncontrolled/fill-related contamination constraints.

Please confirm whether the Environmental Consultant's role is limited to interpreting and incorporating the existing PSI/DSI/RAP into the design, or whether the commission is also to include preparation/revision of the RAP, remedial works specifications, asbestos management documentation, validation planning/reporting and post-remediation site validation.

8) NSW EPA Site Auditor

Please confirm whether an EPA-accredited Site Auditor is required for this project or for Council's Part 5 determination. If required, is the Auditor to be engaged and paid directly by Council, or included within the Lead Consultant's lump sum?

9) Flooding and overland-flow assessment

The additional investigation scope lists a flooding and overland-flow assessment but does not define the modelling level required.

Please confirm whether this requires a project-specific hydraulic/flood model and formal 1% AEP assessment, or whether review of Council's existing flood information together with site grading, stormwater and overland-flow assessment is sufficient. Please also confirm whether existing Council flood models and GIS/model files will be supplied.

10) Sydney Water triple stormwater pipeline information

Council advises that scanning of the triple Sydney Water stormwater pipeline is currently being undertaken and will be provided.

Please confirm when the scan results will be available, the survey/utility quality level to be provided, and whether the information will include surveyed horizontal and vertical positions suitable for detailed design.

11) Sydney Water WSC / Building Plan Approval

The Scope notes that investigations may trigger the need for a Water Servicing Coordinator and formal Sydney Water Building Plan Approval.

Should the tender include engagement of a Water Servicing Coordinator and preparation/management of the Building Plan Approval application, or should this be treated as a separately authorised service if the pipeline investigation confirms it is required?

12) Authority application and statutory fees

Please confirm that Sydney Water, TfNSW, Ausgrid, Sydney Airport and other statutory application, plan-checking, inspection, bond, WAD, ROL, utility connection and authority fees will be paid directly by Council and are not to be included in the Consultant's lump-sum professional fee.

13) TfNSW WAD scope

TfNSW has already indicated concurrence in principle to the access locations/deceleration lane subject to detailed design approval and requires a Works Authorisation Deed, plan-checking fees and potentially a performance bond.

Please confirm whether the Lead Consultant is required to manage the full TfNSW WAD process through approval, including preparation of all TfNSW road design documentation, responses to comments and coordination of the WAD, or only provide the technical design package for Council to administer the WAD.

14) Extent of Foreshore Road works

TfNSW requires left-in/left-out movements, a deceleration lane, crossings and associated road/drainage works to TfNSW requirements.

Please confirm that the Foreshore Road deceleration lane, road widening/kerb works, drainage modifications, signage/linemarking and vehicular crossings form part of the detailed design, IFT and IFC scope.

15) Traffic survey requirements

The Scope lists traffic and parking surveys as potential additional investigations.

Does Council hold recent classified traffic counts, turning movement data, parking demand information or pump-track patronage forecasts? If not, please confirm the type, duration and locations of traffic surveys expected to be included in the tender price.

16) Council-appointed Quantity Surveyor

The Services state that Council will engage a third-party QS for the three concept estimates, 50%, 75% and IFT estimates and the IFT BOQ.

Please confirm that no QS fee is required within the Consultant's lump sum and that the Lead Consultant's obligation is limited to supplying coordinated design information, responding to QS queries and participating in value-management/cost-review activities.

17) Construction “site management plans”

The Services list “site management plans for construction” among the required standard documents.

Please clarify which specific construction site-management plans are to be prepared by the design consultant. We assume contractor SWMS, detailed Construction Environmental Management Plan, Construction Traffic Management Plan, site establishment plan and construction methodology remain the future Contractor's responsibility unless specifically identified otherwise.

18) IFT tender/procurement assistance

The documents are to be used to call construction tenders, after which the Consultant will complete remaining documentation and progress to IFC.

Please confirm whether the consultancy scope includes assistance during the construction tender period, such as responding to tender RFIs, preparing addenda, technical tender evaluations or tender interviews. If so, please nominate the expected tender duration and allowance for RFIs/addenda.

19) IFC trigger and contractor-driven amendments

Please confirm whether IFC is expected to comprise incorporation of Council's final IFT comments and agreed tender clarifications only, or whether redesign arising from the successful contractor's alternative materials, methodologies or value-engineering proposals is also to be included within the lump sum.

20) Additional investigation approval and commercial treatment

Council requires any additional investigations to receive approval before commencement.

Please confirm that investigations identified after review of the existing information but not capable of being reasonably defined at tender stage may be submitted to Council for approval and treated as an additional/provisional service rather than being deemed included in the fixed lump sum.
publicQuestions.answer:
1) Council confirms that a consultant without third-party AS/NZS ISO 9001 certification may submit a conforming tender, provided it can demonstrate an equivalent documented Quality Management System (QMS) acceptable to Council.

Tenderers should provide details of their quality management procedures, including quality assurance processes, document control, independent review/checking procedures and project-specific quality management measures, for Council's assessment.

2) The $2 million construction budget is indicative only and is provided for tendering purposes. The final project budget will be refined as the design develops. For the purposes of preparing fee proposals, the indicative construction budget should be assumed to include all project delivery costs associated with the proposed works, including contamination remediation, Foreshore Road and deceleration lane works, TfNSW-related works, landscape works, lighting and CCTV, authority and approval charges, contractor preliminaries, contingencies and GST. Tenderers should use these assumptions when preparing their submissions.

3) There are no prescribed target dates for individual design milestones. Tenderers are to develop and submit their own programme for delivery of the Services based on the project requirements.

The Consultant is to allow adequate time within its programme for Council review and approval at each stage of the design process. At the submission of the draft Concept Design package, the Consultant is to allow up to twelve (12) weeks for Council review, consideration and endorsement prior to finalisation of the Concept Design. Similarly, at the submission of draft Detailed Design, IFT and IFC packages, the Consultant is to allow up to two (2) weeks for Council review before receiving approval to proceed to the next design milestone.

The twelve (12) week community consultation period may overlap with Council's review period where appropriate. The anticipated process is that the Consultant will prepare a Draft Concept Design incorporating viable options for Council consideration. Council will review and endorse a preferred option, following which a single concept option will be developed for community consultation. Community consultation is anticipated to occur over a period of up to twelve (12) weeks. Feedback received during consultation is to be considered and, where appropriate, incorporated into either the final Concept Design or the subsequent Detailed Design phase, depending on project timing and staging.

The Consultant's final design milestone is the submission of IFC documentation following appointment of the construction contractor and completion of the required IFC review process.

4) The information made available by Council is limited to the documentation included within the Tender Appendix. Tenderers should base their submissions on the information provided and satisfy themselves as to its suitability for the proposed Services.

Where additional survey information is required to complete the design, including feature and level survey, utility investigation, easement verification, cadastral definition or boundary survey, such services are to be included within the Consultant's base scope. Available survey information will generally be provided in PDF and DWG format where available.

Tenderers should assume that any additional survey necessary to support design development, approvals and construction documentation is their responsibility and should be allowed for within their fee proposal.

5) The Tender Appendix includes the existing TfNSW geotechnical information together with Council's more recent site investigation documentation and Remedial Action Plan (B1, B2 and B3). Tenderers are required to review and consider all available information provided as part of the tender documentation.

Council considers the available information to be suitable for concept and preliminary design purposes; however, it should not be relied upon as being sufficient to support detailed pavement design and final construction documentation.

Accordingly, Tenderers shall allow within their base scope for any geotechnical investigations considered necessary to develop and verify the detailed pavement design and complete a final constructable design. This may include, where required, additional test pits, pavement investigations, DCP and/or CBR testing, laboratory testing and associated geotechnical assessment.

6) Tenderers shall allow for supplementary contamination sampling and testing where, following review of the available PSI, DSI and RAP documentation, specific data gaps are identified that are necessary to complete the design and support delivery of a constructable project.

Any investigations that can be reasonably anticipated as being necessary to develop the design, confirm remediation requirements, or support project delivery are to be included within the Consultant's base fee.

Where a service or investigation cannot be reasonably defined at tender stage and its requirement is dependent on findings arising later during project delivery, the Consultant should clearly identify the potential scope within its methodology and provide an indicative provisional allowance. Any such investigations will be subject to Council approval prior to commencement.

7) The Environmental Consultant's role is intended to be limited to interpretation of the existing environmental investigations (including the PSI/DSI and RAP) and incorporation of the identified contamination, asbestos and remediation constraints into the design. Tenderers are to review and rely upon the existing PSI/DSI and RAP documentation provided and allow for the environmental input necessary to inform and support the design.

The scope does not include preparation or revision of the RAP, asbestos management documentation, validation planning or reporting, environmental supervision of remediation works, post-remediation site validation, preparation of remediation completion reports or environmental sign-off.

Notwithstanding the above, where remediation-related requirements affect the design, tender documentation or constructability of the project, the Consultant shall incorporate the requirements of the existing RAP and environmental investigations into the design documentation as appropriate.

Any remediation, asbestos management, validation and associated compliance activities will be undertaken separately.

8) Council does not currently require the engagement of an EPA-accredited Site Auditor as part of this design commission or for the purposes of the Part 5 assessment.

Tenderers are not required to include for the engagement of an EPA-accredited Site Auditor within their fee proposal. Should Council determine that a Site Auditor is required at a later stage due to project approvals, remediation requirements, regulatory advice or other project-specific considerations, the Site Auditor will be engaged separately by Council.

9) The flooding and overland flow assessment is to assess existing flooding and drainage constraints affecting the site and demonstrate that the proposed development will maintain or improve the existing flood and overland flow behaviour of the site and surrounding land.

Council has provided available flood mapping information within the Tender Appendix. Council does not currently have a hydraulic flood model available for tenderers.

Tenderers are to review the available flood information, assess existing and proposed site levels, stormwater drainage design and overland flow paths, and demonstrate that the proposed works will not adversely impact flood behaviour, flood storage, overland flow paths, stormwater drainage performance or adjoining properties.

Tenderers are responsible for determining the level of assessment necessary to support their design. Where the Consultant considers additional hydraulic analysis or flood modelling is necessary to demonstrate compliance with the above requirements, the proposed methodology, assumptions and associated cost allowances should be identified within their submission.

Tenderers should assume that any investigations, analysis or modelling reasonably required to support a constructable design and demonstrate no worsening of flood impacts are included within the base scope of services.

10) Scanning of the Sydney Water triple stormwater pipeline is currently being undertaken by Council. The resulting information will be provided to the successful Consultant at project commencement.

The information will be derived from CCTV inspection and sonde tracing and is expected to include surveyed horizontal and vertical positions of the pipeline suitable for design development. However, Council cannot currently confirm the survey quality level, accuracy or utility quality level classification that will be assigned to the information and tenderers should assume it will be provided in the form received by Council.

The Consultant is responsible for reviewing the information provided and determining whether any supplementary survey, utility investigation, potholing or verification is required to support detailed design, approvals and construction documentation.

Any additional investigations reasonably required to complete a constructable design should be included within the Consultant's base scope.

11) Council understands that the proposed works may interact with existing Sydney Water assets and that approvals may be required from Sydney Water depending on the final design and the outcomes of utility investigations.

Tenderers are to allow for investigation of Sydney Water asset constraints and identification of all relevant approval requirements associated with the proposed works.

At this stage, Council has not confirmed the final approval pathway, including whether a Water Servicing Coordinator (WSC), Building Plan Approval (BPA), Section 73 requirements or other Sydney Water approvals will be required.

Council currently anticipates that a Water Servicing Coordinator will likely be required in relation to the proposed slip lane works over the Sydney Water stormwater main. Additional Sydney Water approvals may also be required if the proposed design includes connection of new stormwater infrastructure to a Sydney Water asset.

Tenderers are to clearly identify any assumptions regarding Sydney Water approvals in their submission and nominate any exclusions from their lump sum fee. Any services excluded from the lump sum should be separately identified with an indicative provisional cost.

12) Authority and statutory application fees are to be paid directly by Council and are not to be included within the Consultant's lump-sum fee.

Where authority applications, approvals, plan checking, inspections, permits, bonds, utility connection charges or other statutory fees are required by Sydney Water, TfNSW, Ausgrid, Sydney Airport or other authorities, the relevant invoice or fee notice is to be provided to Council for direct payment.

The Consultant shall, however, allow for the preparation, coordination and submission of applications and supporting technical documentation required as part of the Services, unless specifically excluded within their proposal.

13) The Consultant is to allow for management of the full TfNSW approval process associated with the proposed works, including coordination of the Works Authorisation Deed (WAD) process, preparation of all required TfNSW road design documentation, responses to TfNSW comments and requests for information, and progression of submissions through to approval.

The Consultant shall act as the primary technical interface with TfNSW throughout the design and approval process and shall incorporate all reasonable TfNSW requirements into the design documentation.

Council may assist with administration and stakeholder liaison activities where required; however, Tenderers should assume responsibility for managing and obtaining the necessary TfNSW technical approvals as part of their base scope.

14) Council confirms that the Foreshore Road works, including the deceleration/slip lane, road widening, kerb and gutter works, drainage modifications, signage, line marking, vehicular access arrangements and all associated civil works required to satisfy TfNSW requirements, form part of the Detailed Design, IFT and IFC scope.

Tenderers are to allow for the preparation, coordination and approval of all road design documentation required by TfNSW and to manage the associated approval process. It is anticipated that the Foreshore Road works will be subject to a separate review and approval process by TfNSW in addition to Council's design review process.

Tenderers should demonstrate previous experience in the design and approval of works within the TfNSW road corridor, including obtaining TfNSW approvals and managing review timeframes associated with external agency approvals.

Tenderers should also recognise that TfNSW approval timeframes may differ from the overall project programme and should plan accordingly. Consultants are expected to demonstrate an understanding of potential project staging and delivery approaches, including scenarios where the car park works may proceed independently while TfNSW review and approval of the Foreshore Road works remains ongoing.

15) Council has not provided traffic count data, turning movement counts, parking demand assessments or patronage forecasts as part of the Tender Appendix.

Tenderers are to engage a suitably qualified traffic consultant as part of their team and allow for all traffic investigations, surveys and reporting necessary to support the design, approvals and delivery of the project.

The scope, location, duration and methodology of any traffic surveys are to be determined by the traffic consultant based on the project requirements and the needs of the proposed development. This is expected to include investigations necessary to support the design and approval of the Foreshore Road slip lane and associated TfNSW approvals, as well as assessment of parking demand, access arrangements, traffic operations and anticipated car park utilisation.

Tenderers should include within their base scope all traffic investigations, surveys, modelling and reporting reasonably required to complete the design and obtain the necessary approvals.

16) No Quantity Surveyor engagement is required to be included within the Consultant's fee proposal. Council will separately engage a Quantity Surveyor to prepare and manage project cost estimates and Bills of Quantities at the nominated project stages.

The Consultant's role is limited to supporting Council and the Council-appointed Quantity Surveyor by providing coordinated design information, responding to QS enquiries, attending coordination meetings where required, and participating in value management and cost review activities necessary to maintain alignment between the design and project budget.

The Consultant shall provide sufficient design information at each project stage to enable the Council-appointed Quantity Surveyor to prepare concept estimates, detailed design estimates and the IFT Bill of Quantities.

17) The reference to "site management plans for construction" relates to plans, assessments and documentation required to support design development, approvals, environmental assessment and delivery planning for the proposed works.

Council does not require the design consultant to prepare contractor-specific construction management documentation. Accordingly, contractor Safe Work Method Statements (SWMS), Construction Environmental Management Plans (CEMP), Construction Traffic Management Plans (CTMP), site establishment plans, detailed construction methodologies, temporary works documentation and similar contractor delivery documents remain the responsibility of the future construction contractor.

The design consultant is required to identify construction constraints, environmental considerations, staging requirements, traffic management considerations and approval requirements as necessary to inform the design, planning approvals, procurement and project delivery.

18) The Consultant will be required to provide assistance during the construction tender period, including assisting Council with responses to tender RFIs and preparation of addenda where updates to the IFT documentation are required.

The scope does not include review of tender submissions, technical tender evaluations, tender interviews, tender clarifications following tender close, or recommendation of a preferred tenderer.

Tenderers should assume a tender period of approximately four (4) to six (6) weeks and allow for up to ten (10) combined RFI responses and/or addenda during that period.

19) The Consultant shall incorporate Council's review comments, approved tender clarifications, and any addenda issued during the tender period into the final documentation.

Tenderers shall also allow for one review and update of the documentation to IFC following appointment of the successful construction contractor.

This review is intended to address coordination, incorporation of agreed contractor comments, constructability matters, and minor adjustments arising from the successful contractor's review of the documentation.

The scope does not include substantial redesign, re-scoping of the project, or multiple iterations resulting from alternative materials, alternative methodologies, value engineering proposals, or contractor-initiated design changes beyond the single IFC review allowance described above.

20) Any additional investigations that are identified by the Consultant following review of the available information, and which could not have been reasonably identified or quantified at the time of tender, are to be clearly documented in the tender delivery or methodology documentation where possible.

Investigations and services that can be reasonably anticipated as being necessary to complete the design, obtain approvals, or deliver a constructable project are to be included within the Consultant's fixed lump sum fee.

Tenderers should clearly state any assumptions regarding additional investigations in their proposal and nominate any associated provisional allowances where appropriate.

publicQuestions.answer: A request for quotation (RFQ) for Quantity Surveying services has not yet been released by Council. Council intends to procure the Quantity Surveying services in the near future.

publicQuestions.question:
Could Council please confirm:

1. Whether the $10 million minimum for PI must be held on an any one claim basis; or

2. Whether a policy providing $5 million any one claim and $10 million in the aggregate satisfies the requirement.

Thank you!
publicQuestions.answer: Council confirms that, for this procurement, a Professional Indemnity policy with a limit of $5 million any one claim and $10 million in the aggregate will satisfy the insurance requirement.

publicQuestions.question:
Can Council please confirm the following:

Is a hydraulic impact assessment required or is a catchment analysis and overland flow check sufficient?

Considering the carpark layout and location is quite developed, are any front end traffic counts or reports required?

Outside of the existing RAP and design in accordance with the RAP what other contaminated land assessments are required?
publicQuestions.answer:
Hydraulic / flooding assessment: Council has provided flood mapping information within the Tender Appendix. The flooding and overland flow assessment is to assess existing flooding and drainage constraints affecting the site and demonstrate that the proposed development will maintain or improve the existing flood and overland flow behaviour of the site and surrounding land. Council does not currently have a hydraulic flood model available. Tenderers are to determine the level of assessment necessary to support the design and demonstrate that the proposed works will not adversely impact flood behaviour, flood storage, overland flow paths, stormwater drainage performance or adjoining properties. Where the Consultant considers additional hydraulic analysis or flood modelling necessary to support these outcomes, this should be included within their methodology and proposal.

Traffic investigations: Tenderers are to engage a suitably qualified traffic consultant and allow for all traffic investigations, surveys and reporting necessary to support the design and approvals process. Council has not provided traffic count data, turning movement counts, parking demand assessments or patronage forecasts as part of the Tender Appendix. The scope and extent of any surveys are to be determined by the traffic consultant, particularly to support the Foreshore Road slip lane design, TfNSW approvals, site access arrangements and assessment of anticipated car park demand and utilisation.

Contaminated land assessments: Tenderers are to review and rely on the existing PSI, DSI and RAP documentation provided. The Environmental Consultant's role is intended to be limited to interpretation of the existing investigations and incorporation of the identified contamination, asbestos and remediation constraints into the design. No revision of the RAP, validation reporting, post-remediation validation or additional contamination assessment is currently required. However, where supplementary contamination investigations are identified as necessary to address specific data gaps and support completion of a constructable design, they are to be included within the Consultant's scope in accordance with the tender requirements.

publicQuestions.question: Good morning, the Schedule of Prices - Lump sum break-up lists the Civil Engineer as the Lead Consultant, however the A1. Scope of Works lists the Civil Engineer as a subconsultant. Can you please confirm who Council prefer as the lead Consultant?
publicQuestions.answer:
Council's preference is for the Civil Engineer to act as the Lead Consultant.

This is fundamentally a civil engineering project, with key project drivers including the car park, Foreshore Road slip lane/deceleration lane works, stormwater drainage, pavement design, utility coordination and associated TfNSW approvals.

The reference in Appendix A1 to various disciplines reflects Council's expectation that Tenderers assemble an appropriately qualified multidisciplinary team. Whilst other lead disciplines may submit a proposal, Tenderers should recognise that both civil engineering and landscape architecture are critical to the successful delivery of the project.

Accordingly, Council expects the Lead Consultant to demonstrate strong capability in managing and coordinating the civil engineering aspects of the project together with the landscape design, approval and stakeholder coordination requirements. The Consultant team should include all necessary specialist subconsultants to deliver the full scope of services.

publicQuestions.question:
The supplied PSI/DSI and RAP identify asbestos-containing material across the site. The RAP states that Council was undertaking a feasibility study to select a preferred remediation option; however, no preferred strategy is identified in the tender documentation.

Please confirm:

1. Whether the remediation feasibility assessment has been completed and, if so, provide the preferred remediation strategy and associated documentation.

2. How access to the site is intended to be managed for the additional site investigations, including any required asbestos controls, and whether tenderers are required to include the associated measures within their fees.
publicQuestions.answer:
1. Council has not selected a preferred remediation strategy at this time. As noted in the RAP, a preferred remediation option has not been finalised. Tenderers should review the RAP and incorporate the identified contamination constraints into the design and methodology. Council's preference is for the design team to consider practical and cost-effective remediation outcomes, including opportunities to integrate remediation measures with the proposed car park construction, where appropriate and consistent with the RAP. No additional documentation relating to a preferred remediation option is currently available.

2. Access to the site for additional investigations will be coordinated by Council. Council's current understanding, based on the PSI/DSI and RAP, is that identified asbestos impacts are generally associated with the stockpiles and shallow surface materials identified in the existing investigations. Tenderers should allow for appropriate asbestos-related health, safety and environmental controls where investigations interact with stockpiled materials or other known asbestos-impacted areas. Any such allowances should be included within the Tenderer's fee proposal. Any services or investigations requiring stockpile manipulation or potential asbestos interaction should be highlighted in the methodology or services delivery.

publicQuestions.question:
1. Does Council have detailed survey of the proposed carpark site? If so, can it be made available for the tender?

2. Referring to the EHO Consulting RAP (Ref JN05247 - RAP - RN18809), has Council undertaken the feasibility study to evaluate all available remedial options? And has a preferred remedial option been determined by Council? If so, can Council advise the preferred remedial option?

3. Can Council advise of the design and documentation budget for the project?

4. Can Council advise of the construction phase budget for the project?

5. Does Council have any preferrence for the software used for hydrology and hydraulic modelling? If yes, can the Council please provide the names of those software?

6. We are Australian subsidiary of an overseas company that has ISO 9001:2025 certification, and we being their subsidiary, follow their ISO 9001 procedures. So, in our response to Schedule of Quality Management System Information, I believe we can provide the audit related information of our overseas parent company. Can Council confirm whether our understanding is correct?

7. Currently we do not have Work Health and Safety Management System certified to ISO 45001 or AS/NZS 4801. Is this a mandatory requirement to bid for the tender?
publicQuestions.answer:
1. Council has made available all survey information currently included within the Tender Appendix. Any available survey information has been provided in the format available to Council. Tenderers should base their submissions on the information provided and satisfy themselves as to its suitability for the proposed Services.

Where additional feature and level survey, cadastral survey, utility investigation, easement verification or other survey information is required to support the design, approvals and preparation of construction documentation, such services are to be included within the Consultant's scope and fee proposal.

2. Council has not selected a preferred remediation strategy at this time. Tenderers are to review the existing PSI, DSI and RAP documentation and incorporate the identified contamination and remediation constraints into the design. Council encourages tenderers to consider practical and cost-effective remediation outcomes that may be integrated with the proposed car park construction where appropriate and consistent with the RAP.

No additional remediation feasibility documentation is available beyond the information included in the Tender Appendix.

3. Council will not disclose the budget allocated for design and documentation services.

4. An indicative construction budget of approximately $2 million has been provided for tendering purposes only. The final project budget will be refined as the design develops and cost planning progresses.

5. Council does not have a prescribed software platform for hydrologic or hydraulic assessment. Tenderers may utilise software considered appropriate by their specialist consultants, provided the methodology, assumptions and outputs are suitable for the project requirements and can demonstrate compliance with relevant industry standards, Council requirements and any approval authority requirements.

6. Council will accept evidence of a parent company's ISO 9001 certification where the tenderer can clearly demonstrate that the certified Quality Management System is implemented, applied and maintained within the Australian entity delivering the Services. Tenderers should provide sufficient supporting information to demonstrate how the certified management system applies to the proposed project team and Australian operations.

Council reserves the right to assess the adequacy of the submitted quality management arrangements as part of the tender evaluation process.

7. No. Council does not require tenderers to hold third-party ISO 45001 or AS/NZS 4801 certification as a mandatory condition of tendering.

Tenderers without certification may submit a conforming tender provided they can demonstrate an equivalent documented Work Health and Safety Management System appropriate for the services being delivered. Tenderers should provide details of their WHS policies, procedures, risk management processes, training arrangements and system implementation measures for Council's assessment.

publicQuestions.question:

4. Council has asked to provide gates on the carpark - what type are they? Simple open/close gates with chain and padlocks - or automated boom gates?

5. Where do we source power supply for lighting and CCTV cameras? Does Council have a preferred/standard make and type of camera (eg Pan/tilt/zoom)? To where will the CCTV film/images be viewed? 6. Can the council mark the TfNSW/Council boundary interface on Figure 1 of the Appendix A.1 and provide for the tender purpose?

7. What are the approximate dimensions of the car park? What is the approximate length of the carpark along Foreshore road?

8. Is the carpark to be built for only light vehicles or heavy vehicles as a Heavy Vehicle Rest Area?
publicQuestions.answer:
1. Tenderers are required to review the existing geotechnical information and determine whether additional investigations are necessary to support detailed pavement design. Council does not consider the existing information to be sufficient for detailed pavement design and final construction documentation. Accordingly, tenderers shall allow within their base scope for any supplementary geotechnical investigations considered necessary, including CBR testing and associated assessment, to develop and verify a constructable pavement design.

2. The purpose of this commission is to develop the concept and detailed design and obtain all necessary approvals associated with the proposed works. Council has undertaken preliminary investigations and discussions with relevant stakeholders, including TfNSW.

However, tenderers should not assume that all approvals have been obtained and are required to allow for the coordination and management of the approvals processes identified within the tender documentation.

3. Council has not prescribed a stormwater disposal solution.

The Consultant is responsible for assessing site conditions, available infrastructure, environmental constraints, utility constraints and approval requirements and developing an appropriate stormwater management strategy as part of the design. Any proposed infiltration measures shall be supported by appropriate technical assessment and demonstrate compliance with relevant standards and authority requirements.

4. Council has not nominated a preferred gate type at this stage.

Tenderers should consider appropriate access control arrangements as part of the concept design process and provide recommendations having regard to operational requirements, safety, maintenance, security and asset lifecycle considerations. The preferred access control arrangement will be determined during the design development process in consultation with Council.

5. Council has not prescribed detailed requirements for power supply, CCTV equipment, communications infrastructure or monitoring arrangements at this stage.

Tenderers are to investigate available servicing opportunities and develop recommendations appropriate for the site and intended operation of the facility. The proposed design should allow for practical, reliable and maintainable solutions consistent with contemporary local government practice and relevant standards. Any specific operational requirements will be developed in consultation with Council during the design process.

6. Council is unable to provide additional cadastral information beyond that contained within the Tender Appendix.

Tenderers are responsible for determining property boundaries, land ownership interfaces and jurisdictional requirements necessary to complete the design and approvals process. Where required, cadastral survey services shall be included within the Consultant's scope.

7. Tenderers should refer to the concept information and documentation included within the Tender Appendix. Council has not prescribed a fixed car park footprint or dimensions.

The final arrangement, capacity and extent of works will form part of the Consultant's design development process and should respond to site constraints, approvals requirements and project objectives.

8. The proposed facility is intended to function as a public car park servicing Sir Joseph Banks Park. Tenderers should assume that the facility is intended for passenger vehicles and associated park users. The project does not include provision of a heavy vehicle rest area or facilities intended for heavy vehicle parking operations.

title: RFT000141- Gympie Regional Council 2026/ 27 In-situ Stabilising Works
description:
Tenders are invited from suitably qualified and experienced contractors to establish schedule rates and pricing for the delivery of in-situ pavement stabilisation works within the Gympie Regional Council local government area. The works form part of the Queensland Department of Transport and Main Roads (TMR) 2026/27 reseal preparation program and are required to improve pavement condition, structural performance, and long-term asset durability prior to the application of reseal treatments.

The scope of work encompasses pavement stabilisation activities on two key transport routes located on the Wide Bay Highway and Gympie Woolooga Road.

The successful contractor will be required to undertake the stabilisation works in accordance with the project specifications, relevant TMR standards, and all applicable legislative and safety requirements. Works are intended to provide a sound and uniform pavement platform suitable for the subsequent resealing operations scheduled under the 2026/27 program.

vendorPanelDetails.buyerDescription:
The Gympie region comprises of eight divisions, represented by the Mayor and eight other councillors (Council).

Within these divisions, Councillors are responsible for a diverse range of portfolios on behalf of their community, including; planning and economic development, disaster management, business, environmental sustainability and water management.

Council plans strategically to ensure services, infrastructure and facilities remain relevant for the community, as well as provide for the needs of a growing resident population.

title: Long Distance Passenger Rail
description:
TMR is seeking a suitably experienced transaction advisor for a confidential rollingstock project. The transaction advisor will be tasked with refining the project’s delivery strategy, developing a transaction strategy and plan, leading the development of all required tender documentation and managing the Registration/Expression of Interest process, including interactions with tenderers and evaluation of all responses.

The initial engagement is for the Readiness for Market phase (indicatively September 2026 – January 2027), with an option for the Procurement phase (indicatively February 2027 – December 2027) included as a separable portion in the Request for Quote documentation. The Procurement phase work scope includes managing the Request for Proposal process, including structured tender interaction and data room management, managing the tender evaluation process and leading the negotiation and contract award strategy and process.

Tenderers must be able to demonstrate experience in similar projects of this nature, including specific capability and experience in rollingstock transactions, and working cooperatively in a team environment with other specialist advisors.

Given the confidential nature of this project, tenderers are requested to complete the attached Confidentiality Deed prior to being issued with the Request for Quote documentation.

Please return the Signed COI to PRS_Tenders@tmr.qld.gov.au

title: REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL 20.26 AIRPORT ADVERTISING LICENSE
description:
The Shire of Ashburton (Shire) invites proposals from suitably qualified and experienced advertising organisations for the provision, management, marketing, sale and ongoing maintenance of advertising opportunities at Onslow Airport and within the surrounding airport precinct.

1.1	Summary of Opportunity

The Shire intends to identify a single advertising organisation (with whom to progress negotiations) at the conclusion of this Request for Proposal process.

The successful Respondent will enter into an exclusivity period of 2 months to endeavour to negotiate a potential licence agreement for advertising space at the Onslow Airport for a 5 year term with an option to extend the term for two (2) x 2 year option periods at the sole discretion of the Shire of Ashburton. It is intended that under this licence agreement (if granted) the successful Respondent will be responsible for developing, installing, managing and commercialising advertising assets across approved locations within the airport environment.

publicQuestions.question:
Will the Principle consider or allow the following:

1.The submission of an alternate or accompanying format price file, for the following reasons:

 a) The Items requested in the price file are quite generalised and will potentially limit the principles’ ability to choose the most appropriate product available, or limit the supplier’s

ability to recommend the most suitable product

b) By allowing alternate or accompanying price/product files, more options will be available to the principle, increasing the ability to achieve a desired result

c) By allowing an alternate format, suppliers will likely be able to update the principle on price variations in a more detailed manner

2. Quarterly updates to product/price files, for the following reasons:

a) Many specified products will fall under agency platforms, meaning price changes and timings will be dictated to by the product suppliers and not the tender suppliers

b) Volatility in fertiliser pricing on the back of the middle east conflict

c) By allowing more regular price reviews, suppliers will be able to ensure best value is being provided to the Principle and will ensure price files are maintained accurately, which is important from an invoicing point of view, and matching the principles PO’s
publicQuestions.answer:
Dear Tenderer,

Thank you for your enquiry regarding SSROC T2026-02 Supply and Delivery of Agricultural Products Services Tender.

In response to your specific questions:

1.	The RFT already contemplates this scenario. Tenderers are reminded of the following provisions that remain in effect:

The Pricing Schedule (Form 7) contained within Part 3-2 Mandatory Returnable Schedules must be completed in full using the prescribed Excel format. The RFT expressly states that “Tenderers must not alter the contents or formatting of the Pricing Schedule, other than to include additional line items where relevant or referred to in the pricing table.” Accordingly, the prescribed Form 7 remains a mandatory conforming requirement and cannot be omitted or replaced.

At the same time, the RFT expressly encourages innovation, stating that “Tenderers are encouraged to submit innovative or alternative ways of servicing this contract.” An alternate or supplementary product/price file may be submitted, provided that:

a.	A fully compliant and conforming Tender, including a completed Form 7, is submitted in the first instance.

b.	The alternate or supplementary file is submitted through Form 22 (Summary of Alternative Tenders) as an alternative or supplementary submission and is clearly identified as such.

c.	The supplementary file is cross-referenced to the relevant line items contained in Form 7.

d.	The alternate file does not replace or contradict the conforming schedule and may only be submitted as a supplement to it.

Tenderers are also reminded that the basket of goods contained in Form 7 is recognised within the RFT as a generic and representative basket only and is not intended to encompass all products that may be procured under the Agreement. Councils may engage Preferred Suppliers for items outside the basket through the SSROC Vendor Panel at the rates and conditions agreed under the PSMA.

2. This matter is governed by the Preferred Supplier Master Agreement (PSMA).

The RFT states that "the Agreement Terms and conditions of pricing, price variations and replacement costs are stipulated in the Preferred Supplier Master Agreement (PSMA)" (Part 4 of the RFT). Tenderers are directed to review the draft PSMA in full.

The formal contract review mechanism includes an Annual Contract Review Report, which encompasses pricing review and market benchmarking as standard components. This represents the primary structured mechanism for price file updates under the Agreement.

Tenderers wishing to propose departures from the pricing variation provisions of the draft PSMA — including any proposal for more frequent (e.g. quarterly) price reviews — are invited to do so via Form 6 (Proposed Contract Departures) in the Part 3-1 Returnable Schedules. Any such departure will be considered by SSROC on its merits and may be subject to negotiation following evaluation. Proposed departures will not render a tender non-conforming, but the Principal reserves the right to accept, reject, or negotiate any proposed departure.

Tenderers proposing a quarterly mechanism are encouraged to include in their Form 6 submission the specific categories or product lines for which the departure is sought, the proposed triggering criteria, and any suggested guardrails (e.g. CPI or index caps, notice periods), to facilitate the Principal's assessment.

Should you require any further clarification, please submit your questions through the tender portal in accordance with the tender process and timelines outlined in the tender documentation.

We thank you for your interest in this opportunity and look forward to receiving your submission.

Q2 - With delivery to a campus where multiple areas are using the linen service is it expected that the provider deliver to each user area or will delivery be to one central point at the campus and collected from this staging area by users

publicQuestions.answer:
Q1. Can you provide more detailed usage information for each site so transport and volumes can be better understood and considered in our offer?

Response:

TAFE Queensland has provided the best available information to support suppliers in preparing their offers. The volumes included within the procurement documentation are indicative only and have been developed for evaluation purposes.

Please refer to Attachment A – Specification and Attachment C – Linen Hire & Laundry Pricing List (Pricing Scenario tab) for indicative demand information.

As outlined in the Specification, service demand varies by campus and is influenced by factors such as student enrolments, training schedules, practical class delivery, events, facility utilisation, and seasonal activity. Accordingly, TAFE Queensland is unable to provide guaranteed site-specific usage volumes. Suppliers should base their offers on their capacity to service nominated locations and accommodate fluctuations in demand throughout the contract term.

The current estimated demand across the TAFE Queensland network is approximately 2,750 to 4,300 items per week; however, actual volumes may be higher or lower depending on operational requirements.

Q2. With delivery to a campus where multiple areas are using the linen service, is it expected that the provider deliver to each user area or will delivery be to one central point at the campus and collected from this staging area by users?

Response:

For the purposes of tender evaluation, suppliers should assume that delivery and collection will occur at a single nominated delivery point within each campus.

Specific delivery arrangements may vary between campuses and service areas and will be confirmed during implementation with the successful supplier(s). Suppliers may identify any assumptions, site requirements, or alternative service delivery approaches within their offer submission.

Q3. Can you clarify what contract term you are seeking to implement with the successful provider, e.g. 1, 2 or 3 years?

Response:

The contract term is stated in both the Invitation to Offer and Attachment A – Specification. The proposed Standing Offer Arrangement term is three (3) years, with an option for TAFE Queensland to extend the arrangement by up to two (2) additional periods of twelve (12) months each, at TAFE Queensland's discretion. The maximum potential term is therefore five (5) years.

title: 2026.31 - Barmaryee Sports Precinct Master Plan
description:
Livingstone Shire Council (Council) invites suitably qualified and experienced consultancy firms to submit a Tender for the preparation of the Barmaryee Multi Sports Precinct Master Plan.

The objective of this engagement is to develop a comprehensive, evidence-based and implementable Master Plan that will guide the future planning, development and staged expansion of the Barmaryee Multi Sports Precinct as a regionally significant sporting and recreation hub.

The Master Plan will establish a long-term vision for the precinct, incorporating the planning and integration of sporting infrastructure, supporting facilities, transport networks, access, parking, open space, landscaping and associated infrastructure to meet current and future community needs.

The Barmaryee Multi Sports Precinct is a strategically important Council-owned facility that currently accommodates a range of sporting and community activities, including Junior Rugby League, Touch Football, Netball, OzTag, Keppel Coast District events and school sporting carnivals.

The precinct has been identified as the preferred location for the future expansion of rectangular sports, including Rugby Union, Outriggers, Volleyball and other compatible sporting and recreation activities. Continued population growth, increasing participation rates and demand for regional sporting infrastructure have created the need for a coordinated and sustainable master planning approach to maximise the precinct's capacity, functionality and long-term value to the community.

The successful Tenderer will be responsible for providing all professional services necessary to deliver the Master Plan in accordance with the Contract, Technical Specification and associated Tender Documents, including project management, stakeholder engagement, site investigations, technical assessments, concept development, implementation planning and final reporting.

The Contract will be administered under AS 4122 – General Conditions of Contract for Consultants, with services delivered in accordance with the staged deliverables specified in the Tender Documents.

publicQuestions.question:
CAD Deliverables Clarification

The tender documentation identifies both the Draft Master Plan and Final Master Plan as requiring submission in CAD format. Could Council please clarify its expectations regarding the CAD deliverable and the intended use of the files?

Our standard approach for strategic master planning is to prepare plans using industry-standard graphic design and publishing software, including Adobe Illustrator and Adobe InDesign. This workflow produces high-quality presentation plans suitable for stakeholder engagement, Council reporting, funding submissions and grant applications, while still allowing accurate spatial planning and design outcomes.

We note that plans prepared directly in CAD software can result in a more technical drawing style and may require additional drafting and graphic production processes to achieve the presentation quality typically expected of master planning documents.

Importantly, Illustrator-based plans can be exported to DWG format, with model space linework and layer information retained and accessible within AutoCAD. As such, it may be possible to satisfy Council's CAD requirements without preparing the master plan entirely within a CAD platform.

Could Council please clarify:

- Whether the requirement for CAD is intended to provide Council with an editable digital file of the final master plan;

- Whether CAD files derived from Illustrator exports would be acceptable;

- Whether Council has a preferred CAD platform or file format (e.g. DWG, DXF); and

- Whether there is a specific operational or asset management purpose for requiring CAD deliverables.

Understanding Council's intended use of the CAD files will assist tenderers in proposing the most appropriate and cost-effective approach to delivering the master plan. Thank you in advance.
publicQuestions.answer:
Council requires the Draft Master Plan and Final Master Plan to be submitted in editable CAD format (DWG) in accordance with the RFQ requirements.

In response to your specific questions:

1. Whether the requirement for CAD is intended to provide Council with an editable digital file of the final master plan

Yes. Council requires editable CAD files of both the Draft and Final Master Plan to support future planning, concept development, staging reviews, grant funding applications and subsequent design activities.

2. Whether CAD files derived from Illustrator exports would be acceptable

Tenderers may utilise their preferred software and workflows during development of the master plan. However, the submitted deliverable must be an editable DWG file that accurately represents the adopted master plan and is suitable for future use and modification by Council and future consultants.

3. Whether Council has a preferred CAD platform or file format

Council requires submission of the Draft and Final Master Plan in DWG format.

4. Whether there is a specific operational or asset management purpose for requiring CAD deliverables

The purpose of the CAD deliverables is to ensure Council retains an editable spatial representation of the adopted master plan that can be utilised for future planning, concept refinement, staging assessments, funding applications and subsequent project development.

Council acknowledges that presentation-quality master plans are often produced using a range of software platforms. However, regardless of the software used during plan development, the Draft and Final Master Plan must be provided as editable DWG files in accordance with the RFQ requirements.

publicQuestions.question:
RFI 1 – Status of Concept Plan Review and Future Facility Provision

Council has provided the Barmaryee Multisport Precinct Concept Plan Review 2024 which identifies preferred future infrastructure including rugby union, AFL, cricket, running track and beach volleyball facilities.

Can Council confirm whether the findings, priorities, facility allocations and future development opportunities identified within the Concept Plan Review represent Council's endorsed strategic position and preferred development direction for the precinct, such that the consultant's role is primarily to validate, refine and spatially accommodate these facilities?

Alternatively, is Council seeking the successful consultant to independently reassess facility requirements, undertake option analysis and prioritisation, and potentially recommend materially different outcomes based on technical investigations, stakeholder consultation, servicing constraints and affordability considerations?

RFI 2 – Sporting Needs Analysis

The Concept Plan Review 2024 references an existing Sporting Needs Analysis used to inform engagement outcomes and future planning for the precinct.

Can Council provide this document to tenderers?

Further, can Council confirm whether the successful consultant is expected to include a specialist sport and recreation consultant to undertake additional participation forecasting, demand modelling or needs assessment activities beyond review of existing Council studies and stakeholder engagement outcomes?

RFI 3 – Stakeholder Engagement Expectations

The Concept Plan Review 2024 identifies previous community surveys, stakeholder engagement activities and direct discussions with sporting clubs and user groups.

Can Council clarify whether the consultant is expected to:

a) validate and refine existing stakeholder requirements; or

b) undertake a new consultation process and re-establish stakeholder requirements from first principles?

Please also clarify the minimum stakeholder engagement activities expected as part of this commission to ensure consistency across tender submissions.

RFI 4 – Cost Planning Scope

The Scope requires preparation of planning-level cost estimates and staging strategies.

Can Council confirm whether cost estimates are required only for the preferred Master Plan outcome, or whether alternative layouts, facility configurations and staging options are also expected to be developed, costed and comparatively assessed?

RFI 5 – Traffic Assessment Scope

Can Council clarify whether the traffic assessment is intended to comprise:

a) a strategic review of site access, circulation and parking requirements to support the Master Plan; or

b) a detailed traffic engineering assessment including traffic generation analysis, intersection performance and future event capacity modelling?

RFI 6 – Flooding and Environmental Assessment Scope

We acknowledge Council's previous responses regarding flood and environmental investigations.

Given the supporting information is not available during the tender period and the extent of any further investigations cannot presently be determined, can Council confirm that:

a) tenderers may assume review of existing information and provision of strategic master planning advice only;

b) any additional flood modelling, hydraulic investigations, ecological field surveys, EPBC Act assessments or specialist studies identified as necessary following review of existing information may be treated as provisional sums or variations?

RFI 7 – Site Servicing Capacity

Has Council undertaken any previous investigations into utility servicing capacity for future expansion of the precinct, including potable water, irrigation water, sewer, electrical and communications infrastructure?

If so, can relevant studies and available servicing information be provided to tenderers?

Further, can Council clarify whether the successful consultant is expected to:

a) undertake a high-level servicing review only; or

b) engage utility authorities and identify network constraints, augmentation requirements and upgrade implications necessary to support the ultimate Master Plan development scenario?
publicQuestions.answer:
RFI 1 – Status of Concept Plan Review and Future Facility Provision

Council confirms that the Barmaryee Multisport Precinct Concept Plan Review 2024 forms the primary basis for preparation of the Master Plan and represents the most recent planning undertaken for the precinct.

The Concept Plan Review 2024 has not been formally endorsed by Council. The consultant is expected to review, validate, refine and optimise the recommendations contained within the Concept Plan Review in accordance with the Scope of Works.

Council is not seeking a new strategic planning exercise or a reassessment of facility requirements from first principles.

RFI2 – Sporting needs analysis

Council will make available relevant background information and previous studies held by Council that are considered applicable to the project. If available, the Sporting Needs Analysis referenced within the Concept Plan Review 2024 will be provided.

Council is not specifically seeking a standalone sporting needs analysis, participation forecasting exercise or demand modelling study. Tenderers should allow within their fee for review of available information, stakeholder engagement and investigations reasonably necessary to satisfy the Scope of Works.

RFI3 – Stakeholder engagement expectations

Council expects the consultant to review previous engagement outcomes and undertake stakeholder engagement activities necessary to validate and refine stakeholder requirements for the Master Plan. Existing consultation outcomes should be considered as key inputs into the process.

The consultant shall engage with the stakeholders identified in the Scope of Works and any additional stakeholders nominated by Council. Tenderers should allow within their fee for all stakeholder engagement activities reasonably necessary to satisfy the Scope of Works.

RFI 4 – Cost Planning Scope

Planning-level cost estimates are required for the preferred Master Plan outcome and associated staging framework. Cost estimates shall be prepared in accordance with the requirements of the Scope of Works and be suitable for strategic planning purposes

RFI 5 – Traffic Assessment Scope

The consultant shall undertake a traffic assessment in accordance with the Scope of Works to inform development of the Master Plan, including consideration of site access, circulation, parking and future precinct requirements. Tenderers should allow within their fee for investigations reasonably necessary to satisfy the Scope of Works.

RFI 6 – Flooding and Environmental Assessment Scope

Existing flood and environmental information held by Council, including the Flood Assessment Report, will be provided where available.

The consultant shall review the information provided and undertake the assessments required by the Scope of Works, allowing within their fee for investigations reasonably necessary to inform development of the Master Plan

RFI 7 – Site Servicing Capacity

Relevant servicing information held by Council will be provided where available.

The consultant shall undertake the servicing assessment required by the Scope of Works and allow within their fee for investigations reasonably necessary to inform development of the Master Plan

Therefore the $20m PL requirement is vastly in excess of the norm for our profession and the cost of increasing ours to that amount would be too onerous to entertain given that there is no assurance of any particular volume of work.

Similarly, although our successfully completed projects have included several major and renowned high-rise buildings, an offshore naval facility, ferry terminals, port and harbour restructuring, shopping centres and similar, our worst-case Professional Indemnity liability is unlikely to ever rise above perhaps $100k, due to the nature of independent checks during the process. All of our output is Checked and Reviewed prior to the fabrication of the steel, by the Architect and Engineer responsible for the project, so any major discrepancies would be corrected at that stage.

A drafting consultancy that engages in projects of the size and scope that we do, would not normally carry PL insurance of more than $5m and PI insurance of $1m, if at all. More than that is excessive for the extent of risk that might ever be encountered, and is also too costly to be viable.

Therefore the question is - can Council vary the insurance requirement on a case-by-case basis, or should we not unnecessary spend our, and Council's, time making and processing this Application?

If the insurance is not variable it would be very unfortunate because over the last 25 years we have built a reputation for providing meticulous product at a price that is more than competitive in our industry

Thank you and kind regards.
publicQuestions.answer:
Good Morning,

Thank you for your enquiry and for providing further information regarding your business.

Council advises that the requirement for Public Liability and Professional Indemnity Insurance is not able to be varied on a case-by-case basis and is outlined at sections 2.3 and 6.3 of Part 2. Scope.

Section 6.3 states:

“The supplier must effect and maintain the following insurances in accordance with the requirements listed for each category at section 2.3:

1.	Public liability insurance in the amount of at least $20,000,000 in respect of any one occurrence and for an unlimited number of claims;

2.	Professional indemnity insurance in the amount of at least $5,000,000 in respect of any one occurrence and for an unlimited number of claims;”

Please refer to section 2.3 to confirm the minimum requirement for insurances at each category.

We appreciate your comments and interest in our procurement and look forward to reviewing your submission should you choose to submit.

Kind regards,

Procurement Team

publicQuestions.question:
--- Q1 - Liability Limit stated in Supplier Engagement Orders ---

Clause 22.1(a) of the Standard Terms and Conditions - Goods and Services limits the aggregate liability of each party to that party's Liability Limit, and clause 1.1(ee)(ii) defines the Supplier's Liability Limit as the amount stated in the SEO. Could Council please confirm what amount, if any, it intends to state as the Liability Limit in Supplier Engagement Orders issued under this register, and whether a standard figure will apply across the register or whether it will be set for each engagement?

--- Q2 - Documents against which departures are recorded ---

Part 3, Schedule F1 asks respondents to provide details of any proposed amendments, qualifications or departures "to the Contract contained in Part 4 - Contract or the scope contained in Part 5 - Scope of the Request for Tender". In this Request for Tender, Part 2 is the Scope and Part 4 is the Schedule of Rates. Could Council please confirm that departures should be recorded against the Standard Terms and Conditions - Goods and Services (Issue LGT2.4, October 2025) and Part 2. Scope?

--- Q3 - GST treatment of the Schedule of Rates ---

Section 5.3 of Part 2 - Scope requires hourly rates to be charged inclusive of GST, and the Part 4 column headings read "GST Inc". Clause 5.3 of the Procurement Process Conditions requires the Price to be submitted exclusive of GST, and clause 16.10 of the Standard Terms and Conditions provides that the amount payable for a supply is to be increased by the amount of any GST imposed. Council has previously confirmed that rates are to be submitted GST inclusive. Could Council please also confirm that no further GST will be added to those rates on invoice under clause 16.10?
publicQuestions.answer:
Thank you for your enquiry.

--- Q1 - Liability Limit stated in Supplier Engagement Orders ---

This Arrangement does not, in itself, constitute a contract for the provision of Goods and/or Services, and therefore a liability limit is not predetermined for future procurements.

Clause 1.1(ee) Liability Limit and Clause 1.1(xx) SEO (from ‘Supplier Engagement Order’) provide the mechanism for the applicable liability limit to be established for each future procurement, with the Supplier’s liability determined in accordance with Clause 1.1(ee) and the relevant SEO.

--- Q2 - Documents against which departures are recorded ---

The references to Part 4 – Contract and Part 5 – Scope are to the respective Parts identified in the Request for Tender documentation. Respondents are to record any proposed amendments, qualifications or departures against the relevant Contract and Scope documents identified in the Request for Tender.

--- Q3 - GST treatment of the Schedule of Rates ---

Council advises that, for the purposes of completing the Schedule of Rates, all rates are to be submitted inclusive of GST, as indicated in Part 4 – Schedule of Rates, where the relevant rate columns are identified as “Rate (Inc GST)”.

Accordingly, Respondents should ensure that their tendered rates are inclusive of GST. For clarity, the Schedule of Rates is to be relied upon in determining the required GST treatment of the tendered rates, and the rates submitted are not to have GST added again on invoicing.

Kind regards,

Procurement Team

title: Supply and Delivery of One Articulated Motor Grader
description:
Central Goldfields Shire Council invites tenders for the supply and delivery of one (1) new articulated diesel-powered Motor Grader for use in municipal road construction, renewal and maintenance throughout the Central Goldfields Shire municipality.
