Dear Procurement officer,

We have the following questions. If you could please provide clarification on the queries below, it would be greatly appreciated, as this information will assist us in preparing and submitting our tender response.

1. RFID driver sign-on and start inhibit on the existing system

Section 1.2 lists RFID driver sign-on with asset start inhibit as a minimum requirement. Is that capability currently wired and enabled across the existing fitted assets, or is it a capability of the installed system that has not been commissioned? If it is not currently enabled, should a proposal to support the existing system include pricing to retrofit it?

2. Existing employee card technology

Council has advised that the existing RFID readers encode Wiegand 26 with parity 4, and that the same employee cards are used for building access. Wiegand 26 describes the reader to panel wire format rather than the card technology, so it does not identify the card itself. Could Council confirm the operating frequency and card technology of the existing employee cards, for example 125 kHz proximity such as HID Prox or EM4102, or 13.56 MHz such as MIFARE Classic or DESFire. The answer determines the method for adding an individually identifiable credential to the existing cards without disturbing building access.

3. The twelve month history requirement

Section 1.2 requires that the system can historically track assets up to 12 months. Does Council intend this as a forward-looking data retention capability from the commencement of the contract, or does it require migration of the existing 12 months of historical telematics data into the new system? If migration is required, will Council provide an export of the existing data or arrange for the incumbent to do so?

4. Removal of the existing hardware

Where a proposal involves migration to a new system, does Council require the existing telematics hardware to be removed and returned to Council, and where should the cost of that removal be shown in Schedule B2, which does not include a removal line item?
publicQuestions.answer:
Good afternoon and thank you for your questions

1. RFID driver sign-on and start inhibit on the existing system

Section 1.2 lists RFID driver sign-on with asset start inhibit as a minimum requirement. Is that capability currently wired and enabled across the existing fitted assets, or is it a capability of the installed system that has not been commissioned? If it is not currently enabled, should a proposal to support the existing system include pricing to retrofit it? This system is fitted and operation on all existing units

2. Existing employee card technology

Council has advised that the existing RFID readers encode Wiegand 26 with parity 4, and that the same employee cards are used for building access. Wiegand 26 describes the reader to panel wire format rather than the card technology, so it does not identify the card itself. Could Council confirm the operating frequency and card technology of the existing employee cards, for example 125 kHz proximity such as HID Prox or EM4102, or 13.56 MHz such as MIFARE Classic or DESFire. The answer determines the method for adding an individually identifiable credential to the existing cards without disturbing building access. Our existing cards are HID Prox. Our existing Mix Telematics system and all other systems that utilise our employee RFID cards can use all 3 of these credential types

3. The twelve month history requirement

Section 1.2 requires that the system can historically track assets up to 12 months. Does Council intend this as a forward-looking data retention capability from the commencement of the contract, or does it require migration of the existing 12 months of historical telematics data into the new system? If migration is required, will Council provide an export of the existing data or arrange for the incumbent to do so? New suppliers are not required to provision for the existing historical 12 months of data. New suppliers are required to maintain a minimum rolling 12 months historical tracking data from implementation date moving forward.

4. Removal of the existing hardware

Where a proposal involves migration to a new system, does Council require the existing telematics hardware to be removed and returned to Council, and where should the cost of that removal be shown in Schedule B2, which does not include a removal line item? For a migration proposal, the implantation plan should include removal of the existing system. The proposal should include a labour time per unit removal. This would then be applied using the rate “Labour - Repair and Rectification work” on schedule B2

title: Request for Quote – Tim Fischer Bridge & Heavy Vehicle Monitoring
description:
The Department of Transport and Main Roads (TMR) invites suitably qualified suppliers to submit a quotation for CN-27671 – STR26749 Tim Fischer Bridge & Heavy Vehicle Monitoring.

Location: Wide Bay Burnett Region, Queensland

Key Details

RFQ Closing Date: 5:00 pm, Wednesday, 9 September 2026

Submission Requirements

Suppliers are required to complete Section 2 – Supplier Response of the CN-27671 – STR26749 Request for Quote document and submit a quotation addressing the evaluation criteria outlined in the RFQ and engagement brief. Responses must demonstrate the supplier’s capability to deliver the services in accordance with the specifications and scope of work provided.

Scope of Services

Engineering and Technology Branch is seeking to engage a specialist contractor (the Offeror) with demonstrated expertise in structural monitoring and data collection services to support the Tim Fischer Bridge & Heavy Vehicle Monitoring Project within the Wide Bay Burnett Region.

The services will involve the collection, retrieval and reporting of bridge monitoring data to support project objectives. Further details of the requirements are provided in the Request for Quote and Engagement Brief.

publicQuestions.question:
Of the 1600 heavy vehicles per day, is there an estimate for the number of threshold 1 and 2 exceedances? This is for data storage and 4G transmission requirements.

Can TMR confirm the expected award date for the contract? Given the 3-week notice periods for site access and end of October delivery date, sensor selection will need to consider lead times.

Confirm if a certain level of accuracy is required for the temperature sensors.

Can nominal distances and expected (or max/min) measurement ranges for the displacement sensors be provided, and their required accuracy.

For the optional number plate detection, is a camera with combined ANPR and suitable optics acceptable? Or is the footage to capture number plates for human review?
publicQuestions.answer:
Q. Of the 1600 heavy vehicles per day, is there an estimate for the number of threshold 1 and 2 exceedances? This is for data storage and 4G transmission requirements.

A. The number of Threshold 1 and Threshold 2 exceedances will depend on the final trigger levels adopted. As a guide, TMR aims to capture waveform data for responses exceeding those typically generated by a heavy vehicle of approximately 20 tonnes. For video capture, a lower trigger frequency may be appropriate. Suppliers may assume that approximately the largest 1% of responses would be captured, equating to around 16 events per day based on the expected traffic volume of 1600 heavy vehicles per day.

Q. Can TMR confirm the expected award date for the contract? Given the 3-week notice periods for site access and end of October delivery date, sensor selection will need to consider lead times.

A. The anticipated contract award date is approximately two weeks after the RFQ closing date, subject to evaluation outcomes and internal approvals.

Q Confirm if a certain level of accuracy is required for the temperature sensors.

A. A temperature sensor resolution of 0.01°C is required. No specific accuracy requirement has been mandated; however, suppliers should provide details of proposed temperature sensors including the accuracy

Q. Can nominal distances and expected (or max/min) measurement ranges for the displacement sensors be provided, and their required accuracy.

A. Pier 5 has a 375mm slotted hole in the expansion joint restraint angle. A longitudinal displacement sensor measurement range of approximately 400 mm, and transverse and vertical displacement sensor measurement ranges of approximately 50 mm are recommended. Suppliers may propose alternative ranges with justification.

Q. For the optional number plate detection, is a camera with combined ANPR and suitable optics acceptable? Or is the footage to capture number plates for human review?

A. Both approaches are acceptable. A camera with integrated ANPR capability is preferred where available; however, the system does not mandate ANPR functionality. The camera should provide image/video footage of sufficient quality to allow manual number plate identification and verification when required.

publicQuestions.question:
1 - Can you please provide drawings of the bridge? Specifically looking for drawing around the piers, expansion joints, and bearings where sensors are located to determine suitable mounting brackets and associated ancillaries.

2 - Can you please provide close up photos of the bearings, piers, and expansion joints around where sensors are to be located?

3 - Page 8 of the brief lists the specifications for the tilt sensors as 0.001m/m resolution required, while page 10 lists 0.0001m/m resolution required. The latter seems unnecessarily high. Can you please confirm required tilt sensor accuracy?

4 - Time Synchronisation requirements - Do you require all instruments to be time synchronized together (to within the 100Hz tolerance), and trigger together? For example, a vehicle that exceeds the threshold for a sensor at span 1 and begins data capture, will also cause simultaneous capture of data from sensors at span 5 at the same instant.

Or is it acceptable for a span 5 sensor to only capture data if its local threshold is exceeded, irrespective of whether readings are occurring on other spans?

5 - The brief mentions a buried battery (Wom-Bat) with solar panels on the pole near Abut A. Is a buried battery and solar panel off the bridge required, or are we free to propose an alternative with solar panels mounted to the bridge pier headstock?

6 - Site working hours are listed as 7pm to 5am (night works). Will TMR/RoadTek be providing temporary site lighting and site facilities (i.e. laydown area, toilet) during this period, or are we to include these in our scope?
publicQuestions.answer: Refer to attachments uploaded 04/09/2026.

publicQuestions.question:
Q1. Engagement Brief, The uni-axial tilt sensor resolution is stated as 0.001 m/m in the Figure 5 legend and as 0.0001 m/m in the Instrumentation details table.

Q2. Strain sensor resolution is specified as 0.1 microstrain. The Scope table refers throughout to strains "relative to unloaded background strains", which indicates a dynamic (event-relative) measurement. Please confirm that 0.1 microstrain is a dynamic resolution requirement rather than an absolute accuracy requirement sustained over the monitoring period.

Q3. No measurement ranges are specified for the displacement sensors. Please confirm the expected movement ranges, or confirm that the Offeror may nominate them, for (a) girder to restraint angle vertical, longitudinal and transverse movements, and (b) longitudinal movement across the Pier 5 expansion joint under the full seasonal thermal range.

Q4. The location of the four provisional piezo sensors is stated as Span 5 in the Scope and in the Instrumentation details table, and as Span 4 in the Fee structure table. Please confirm the correct span.

Q5. The Figure 4 legend reads "Camera 25fps + Scene camera + Illumination", which may indicate two separate camera units, whereas the Instrumentation details table states a quantity of one. Please confirm the required number of camera units.

Q6. The provisional piezo sensors require a saw-cut slot in the deck running surface. Please confirm that TMR accepts this intervention to the wearing surface, confirm the reinstatement standard required, and confirm that TMR will provide and pay for the lane closure and traffic management required for deck-level works. The Excluded section addresses traffic control associated with access by UBIU or EWP, which is a different operation.

Q7. The deck top temperature sensors are to be located 30 mm below the top surface of the deck. Please confirm that coring of the running surface and any waterproofing membrane is permitted, confirm the reinstatement detail required, and confirm that TMR will provide the lane closure and traffic management for this work, which cannot be undertaken from beneath the bridge.

Q8. Please clarify the extent of Provisional item 7. In particular whether it comprises transfer of title in the installed hardware, confirm what is intended by "monitoring logic" whether a perpetual licence to the configured logger programs and processing logic, delivery of source, or both — and whether any continuing access to the data platform is required.

Q9. The reference system describes a buried battery adjacent to the pole. Please confirm which party is responsible for excavation approvals, service location (Before You Dig Australia), and any environmental or cultural heritage clearances required for excavation within the road reserve.

Q10. Please confirm that TMR will provide the calibration vehicle, its driver, traffic management and a certified weighbridge docket for the vehicle mass, and confirm the expected duration of the calibration exercise so that a consistent allowance can be made across offers.

Q11. The reference system specifies three days of battery autonomy without charge. In this locality the summer wet season can produce longer periods of heavy overcast. Would TMR wish a five-day or seven-day autonomy options to be priced separately?

title: Bamaga Football Oval Lighting
description:
The Northern Peninsular Area Council is looking to upgrade the lighting at the Bamaga Football Oval to Queensland Rugby League Seniors standards (200 Lux).

There are existing lighting poles at the ground, but it would be preferable to replace these with poles that can be lowered for maintenance. NPARC will consider multiple options from suppliers to achieve the 200 Lux standard for the lowest lifecycle cost.

Automatic and remote control of the lights is desirable.

The lights must be installed prior to the start of the 2027 football season - say 1 June 2027. Remembering that the wet season makes travel and construction works difficult from December to April each year.

This is a design and construct project. NPARC would be willing to evaluate a number of proposals from each supplier.

vendorPanelDetails.background:
The Northern Peninsular area is a proud Rugby League Area and competition in the area is strong for men's, women's and children's competitions.

The Bamaga Oval has undergone a number of upgrades over the past year, and the new lights will make this a first-class facility.

I have been getting multiple enquiries about downloading the documents for this tender. There are no documents to download.

I could not find any historical information on the current lighting system at the oval.

This should not be relevant to this proposal as we are looking for a completely new system, not using any of the current lighting system, other than the electrical conduits and pits may be of use for the new system. Again, I have no drawings to show where those pits and conduits are.

The existing lights will be moved by NPARC to the Injinoo Oval (if feasible).

The Northern Peninsular Area Council is looking to upgrade the lighting at the Bamaga Football Oval to Queensland Rugby League Seniors standards (200 Lux).

There are existing lighting poles at the ground, but it would be preferable to replace these with poles that can be lowered for maintenance. NPARC will consider multiple options from suppliers to achieve the 200 Lux standard for the lowest lifecycle cost.

Automatic and remote control of the lights is desirable.

The lights must be installed prior to the start of the 2027 football season - say 1 June 2027. Remembering that the wet season makes travel and construction works difficult from December to April each year. 

This is a design and construct project. NPARC would be willing to evaluate a number of proposals from each supplier.

title: Register of Prequalified Suppliers for Plant and Truck Hire
description:
Cassowary Coast Regional Council invites tenders from a variety of suitably qualified and experienced Tenderers for appointment as a pre-qualified supplier of the wet hire (with operator) and dry hire (without operator) of plant and truck hire.

The Principal provides a range of construction and maintenance services on the Principal’s existing infrastructure assets that require the use of various plant and equipment. Pre-qualified suppliers will be used to supplement the Principal’s own equipment and resources.

vendorPanelDetails.buyerDescription: The Cassowary Coast Region is a local government area in the Far North Queensland region of Queensland, Australia, south of Cairns and centred on the towns of Innisfail, Cardwell and Tully. It was created in 2008 from a merger of the Shire of Cardwell and the Shire of Johnstone.
vendorPanelDetails.queryCutoffAtRaw: Sunday 06 September 2026 04:00 PM (E. Australia Standard Time)
vendorPanelDetails.background:
The selection of a Tenderer as a pre-qualified supplier entitles the Principal to engage the Tenderer during the Term without first seeking quotes or tenders but does not give rise to any obligation on the Principal to do so. Selection as a pre-qualified supplier does not guarantee that the Tenderer will be engaged to provide any, or any minimum quantity or value of, services. The engagement of a successful Tenderer will be at the Principal’s sole discretion based on operational requirements.

Suppliers who were successfully appointed to the Register of Prequalified Suppliers for Plant and Truck Hire in 2024 and 2025 are not required to submit a tender again this year, as this is the same register. This process provides an opportunity for those not currently on the register, to submit a Tender for inclusion.

publicQuestions.question:
Our organisation is an existing successful supplier under this tender arrangement, and we note the advice that existing successful suppliers are not required to resubmit as part of the supplier refresh process.

Could you please clarify whether existing panel suppliers are permitted to submit improved pricing for consideration as part of the supplier refresh process?

If so, could you please confirm the preferred method for providing updated pricing and any supporting information? In particular, would suppliers be required to resubmit the full tender, including all response schedules, or would an updated pricing schedule be sufficient?

Thank you for your guidance.
publicQuestions.answer:
Thank you for your enquiry.

Council intends to communicate directly with existing suppliers of the Register of Prequalified Suppliers for Truck and Plant Hire (COW000100) to advise them of the opportunity to submit revised pricing.

This upcoming opportunity will be conducted separately from this Request for Tender. Further information will be provided to existing suppliers in due course.

Kind regards,

Procurement Team

publicQuestions.question:
Good Afternoon,

We've been successful on the ROPS COW000100 last year, however we have not yet received any contract from Council.

Do we require to re-tender again this time?

Thank you.
publicQuestions.answer:
Good Afternoon,

Thank you for your enquiry.

Council can confirm that Suppliers who were successfully appointed to the Register of Prequalified Suppliers for Plant and Truck Hire in 2024 and 2025 are not required to submit a Tender again this year, as this is the same register. This process provides an opportunity for those not currently on the register, to submit a Tender for inclusion.

Kind Regards,

Procurement Team

publicQuestions.question:
We are currently reviewing the requirements with the intention of submitting a response and would appreciate it if Council could provide, or direct us to, a current list of the plant, trucks and equipment typically required under this register.

Where available, could you please include the preferred makes, models, sizes/capacities and specifications for the equipment Council may require. This will assist us in identifying suitable equipment within our existing fleet and through our supply network that meets Council's operational requirements.

KFI Group has access to a broad range of heavy plant, trucks and support equipment, and we are keen to understand Council's requirements so we can put forward the most suitable equipment and competitive rates as part of our submission.
publicQuestions.answer:
Thank you for your enquiry.

Council operates a decentralised procurement model, with individual departments and officers responsible for procuring plant, trucks and equipment based on their operational requirements. As such, Council is unable to provide a definitive list of preferred makes, models, sizes, capacities or specifications.

Suppliers are encouraged to nominate any plant, trucks and equipment they consider suitable for inclusion on the Register, provided the equipment meets the requirements and categories outlined in Part 2. Scope.

You may include equipment from your existing fleet and/or equipment available through your supply network. Council will consider the equipment and rates submitted in accordance with the requirements of the Register.

Kind regards,

Procurement Team

This process provides an opportunity for those not currently on the register, to submit a Tender for inclusion.

Council intends to communicate directly with existing suppliers of the Register of Prequalified Suppliers for Truck and Plant Hire (COW000100) to advise them of the opportunity to submit revised pricing and any requirements.

Kind regards,

Procurement Team

publicQuestions.question:
RFI – COW000100 – GST Treatment of Tendered Rates

Ref: Scope cl 5.3; Procurement Process Conditions cl 5.3; Part 4 – Schedule of Rates

The RFT documents conflict on GST treatment: Scope cl 5.3 says rates are to be inclusive of GST; Procurement Process Conditions cl 5.3 says the Price must be exclusive of GST; and the Schedule of Rates columns are headed "Rate (Inc GST)."

Please confirm whether rates should be submitted GST-inclusive or GST-exclusive, and whether an addendum will issue.
publicQuestions.answer:
Thank you for your enquiry.

Council advises that, for the purposes of completing the Schedule of Rates, all rates are to be submitted inclusive of GST, as indicated in Part 4 – Schedule of Rates, where the relevant rate columns are identified as “Rate (Inc GST)”.

Accordingly, Respondents should ensure that their tendered rates are inclusive of GST. For clarity, the Schedule of Rates is to be relied upon in determining the required GST treatment of the tendered rates.

Kind regards

Procurement Team

title: Provision of a Signage Design Manual
description:
The City of Clarence is seeking an experienced environmental graphic designer or signage design specialist to develop a practical and contemporary Signage Design Manual that provides a consistent, accessible and durable approach to signage across Council-managed places and facilities. The Manual should provide clear design and technical guidance so Council can design, procure, install, maintain and progressively replace standard signage across Clarence.

It is desirable that the consultant has demonstrated experience in city-wide or local government signage systems, including design strategy, documentation and implementation guidance.

The purpose of this project is to develop and implement a comprehensive Signage Design Manual for the City of Clarence. The manual will ensure that future public signage across the city is consistent, clear, and effective, aligning with urban design best practice, accessibility standards, and the visual identity of City of Clarence.

This manual will serve as a key reference for the design, placement and maintenance of signage across all Council-managed assets and public spaces, supporting a cohesive and welcoming city experience for residents and visitors alike.

The public spaces, facilities, and assets within City of Clarence are currently signed using a wide range of designs, materials, and messaging approaches. This has resulted in an inconsistent visual identity and, at times, confusion for the community. The absence of clear, consolidated design standards impacts communication, accessibility and a consistent maintenance approach.

To address these challenges and plan proactively for a growing and evolving community, we want to develop a new Signage Design Manual that:

•	Establishes a clear and consistent visual style for all signage

•	Reflects the character, identity and values of the City of Clarence

•	Improves user experience, wayfinding and accessibility

•	Provides practical design and implementation guidance for future projects

This project is being undertaken at a pivotal time. We have revised our 10-year Strategic Plan, are progressing a place branding project and are renewing our Signage Policy. We have recently refreshed our brand to bring its visual style into the modern era and endorsed a Reconciliation Action Plan and Customer Experience Strategy.

Many of the City’s current signs are aged or outdated, reinforcing the need for a coordinated, forward-looking approach. The new manual will also incorporate flexibility for emerging technologies such as digital and interactive signage and allow for future brand evolution if required.

CLOSE OF QUOTATIONS

3pm, Wednesday 09 September 2026

LATE QUOTATIONS WILL NOT BE ACCEPTED

publicQuestions.question: Will the place brand be completed - or nearing completion - when this project begins? Place brand regularly has an impact on signage - there will be occasions where the preference for future signage is place brand eg a 'mixed audience' sign like wayfinding, entry signs or interpretative, and the place brand often works well to lead the visuals for these. It would be great to look at this project through a place and Council brand lens and develop a strategy that considers both, but understand the timing may not align.
publicQuestions.answer:
Good Morning,

Yes - the place brand project in in the design stage currently and we expect to see some of the design principles within a month or two. Further discussion will follow however we will be able to brief the signage manual designer on this process and keep them informed of its progress.

publicQuestions.question: Will we be able to work with Council and/or preferred sign print and install suppliers to define things like fabrication specifications, installation specifications and material standards? As these differ from Council to Council and sometimes supplier to supplier, so we would want strong input from Council ont his.
publicQuestions.answer:
Good Morning,

It is the expectation that the designer will work with Council on this and once we have some options, these could be tested with a few suppliers to ensure ease of fabrication, and test costs involved.

publicQuestions.question: The RFQ states that an 'existing signage audit' is out of scope. However understanding the existing signage is critical to success of a new approach. Will Council be able to provide an audit, or at least examples of existing signs?
publicQuestions.answer:
Good Morning,

We can provide a full range of examples of the type of signs the manual needs to address - please note this project does not extend to road signage. In general, we'd like the manual to provide a series of standard sizes and designs - based on good practice signage standards - rather than re-create what is currently across the city.

publicQuestions.question: The deliverables include 'fabrication-ready files'; can we please confirm that's only for the examples that are designed for the manual? Not final, production-ready artwork for every current Council sign? As 'fabrication-ready' would generally mean it has all the final information in place, approved, and ready to print, whereas a design manual is more for examples than finished artwork.
publicQuestions.answer:
Good Morning,

The signage manual is intended to provide templates/examples which can be applied across all signage to standardise our signage

Council want to make sure we have design files, logos/fonts that we can then use to prepare our own sign proofs in house to be fabricated by signage suppliers.

publicQuestions.question: Are you able to provide any guidance on budget? Projects like this have huge budget ranges based on number of design examples, number of design concepts required, expected size of design manual, so if you can provide even a budget range, or upper limit, that would be ideal.
publicQuestions.answer:
Good Afternoon,

Thank you for your enquiry.

Council is unable to disclose the budget or budget range for this project.

Warm Regards,

Rebecca Riseley

publicQuestions.question:
Existing signage understanding :

Could you please provide more detail on the required level of investigation and understanding of the existing signage that’s required. Does the Council expect a site visit by the consultant or will the Council supply photographic records?

Number of templates:

For pricing purposes we have assumed approximately 26 individual sign templates in total, distributed as follows: Informational (3), interpretive (5), tracks and trails (6), directional and wayfinding (5), regulatory and warning (7). Can Council confirm this is a reasonable basis or advise a preferred number?

Fabrication-ready files :

Does Council require dimensioned, production-ready artwork per template (e.g. vector artwork with cut lines, panel sizes, substrate call-outs) suitable for issue directly to a fabricator, or design intent drawings that a fabricator would then shop-detail?

'Design drawing template':

Can you please specify the deliverables for the ‘design drawings/templates’ line item?

Template content and character limits:

For the design templates, we have assumed the Council will provide final sign content, and that our deliverable is a template with defined text zones and maximum character counts per zone (rather than the written content itself). Can Council confirm this, or advise if drafting sign copy is expected to sit within our scope?

On interpretive content specifically:

Interpretive signage is listed at a number of sites. We have assumed the deliverable is the interpretive template and content structure, and that the historical research, copywriting and any associated heritage or cultural consultation for site-specific consultation are excluded. Can Council confirm this? If interpretive content development is required, could Council indicate the number of sites and whether existing research material is available?

Aboriginal place names and cultural interpretation:

Contract Schedule 1 requires the design system to accommodate Aboriginal place names, language and cultural interpretation "including consultation requirements." We have assumed our deliverable is documenting the consultation protocol and approval pathway within the Manual, and that Council will lead, fund and manage any direct engagement with the community and relevant Aboriginal organisations. Can Council confirm this? If the consultant is expected to convene that engagement, could Council advise which organisations it works with and whether existing protocols or agreements are in place under the Reconciliation Action Plan?

Installation specifications:

What level of detail on installation is required for each signage type? Are we to assume these will all be installed in ground? do we need to provide recommendations for both? Does the Council have existing standard pole/fitting details to align to?

Icons and pictograms:

Will Council provide icons and pictograms, or is sourcing and creating these assets part of the consultant's scope?

Braille:

Is braille required across the entire suite of templates? Is the contractor to supply fabrication specifications for braille signage?

Workshops and meetings:

How many workshops and meetings are allocated as part of the project? Are they required to be in person? And if so, where would they be held?
publicQuestions.answer:
Good Morning,

Existing signage:

Council are able to provide some images of the types of signs we have across the city; however, we expect some level of site investigation by the consultant will be beneficial to understand the landscape of signage.

Number of templates:

This is a reasonable basis.

Fabrication-ready files:

Council would like templates of final artwork - editable files which includes exact dimensions, bleeds, vector artwork etc.

'Design drawing template':

This refers to:

•	Visual concepts showing what the finished item will look like

•	Dimensions and proportions

•	Layouts for each sign/panel/item

•	application of our visual brand guide

•	Materials or finishes

•	Templates that can be reused for future items

•	Files supplied in particular formats (e.g. Illustrator, InDesign)

•	And Installation requirements

Template content and character limits:

Yes, it is confirmed council will generate final content for the signage

On interpretive content specifically:

Correct, all historical research, copywriting or consultation is excluded from this project. Council would hope to have space for interpretative signage options on some of the templates.

Aboriginal place names and cultural interpretation:

Council will coordinate any Aboriginal place name content, approval and details. We would simply seek that there are provisions for this to be featured on some of the signage templates. Additionally, it has been indicated Council wants the designer to see if there were opportunities to link to the Reconciliation Action Plan (this may relate to colors/themes/artwork/acknowledgement of Country).

Installation specifications:

Most of our city signage are fitted to the ground in our open spaces. Guidance on how these are to be installed would be preferred (i.e. height or signposts to keep sign at eyeline). This is a requirement of the project to have the manual specify the height, size, post and installation requirements so that signage is consistent and uniform in appearance and height datum in the landscape.

Icons and pictograms:

Yes - council can provide icons where needed and within visual branding guidelines, however there may be additional icons that we need to get assistance with.

Braille:

No.

Workshops and meetings:

In Person either in council offices or in Hobart. Over video call can also be considered for the right candidate.

publicQuestions.question: Is it ok to provide the whole response in a different format eg branded PDF, as long as the 'Quotation Form' section follows the same content structure as the Word document provided?
publicQuestions.answer:
Good Afternoon,

Council will accept the part 5 agreement in another format so long as it contains every question and section of the part 5 including the signing block.

Should parts of the part 5 be missed/not included it may mean the submission is non-conforming or scores poorly.

Council will also accept the part 5 in its original format with directions to go to a specific part of the response e.g. under Third-party quality accreditation "please see appendix 2"

publicQuestions.question: Can you please clarify what is meant by 'Number of lost time injuries', followed by 'Number of person days on contract', followed by 'Total days lost due to injuries' in criterion 2B? These don't feel relevant to this type of project and we've certainly never had lost time injuries in previous projects as a design agency, but if it needs to be filled out can you please let us know what we should put in each section?
publicQuestions.answer:
Good Afternoon,

number of lost time injuries - was there any injuries that caused a loss of time to the contract

number of person days on contract - how many days did you work on the listed contract

total days lost due to injuries - did any of the above lost time injuries result in days' worth of loss.

e.g. 2 lost time injuries - 240 days on contract - resulted in 4 days lost due to injuries.

Should these metrics be available please include them in your response. Should they not be available you will not be penalised for leaving this particular section blank however you should be able to provide the number of days you were on the contract.

vendorPanelDetails.background:
The Sunshine Coast Stadium (SCS) is a major regional sporting and events facility that supports community participation, high-performance sport and the delivery of large-scale events.

The SCS has been identified as a host venue for 2032 Brisbane Olympic and Paralympic Games, necessitating upgrades to meet Games requirements and support increased future demand.

The Sunshine Coast’s home of big events will be bigger and better with an upgrade to SCS, securing its position as the region’s premier venue for local, national and international sporting, leisure and entertainment events.

The stadium upgrade will boost permanent seating with a new eastern grandstand and a rebuilt western grandstand. Upgrades will include multi-purpose community spaces and amenities accessible to people of all abilities.

The early design vision by awarded Principal Consultant, Architectus, is inspired by the Sunshine Coast’s natural landscape and coastal lifestyle. Initial concepts explore light, open forms, shaded concourses and elevated seating to create a relaxed, immersive game-day experience.

The sports fields at SCS support a range of activities, from grassroots community sport to elite training camps and national-level football, rugby league, and rugby union games.

The planned upgrades will deliver modern, high-quality facilities for athletes, officials, and fans, ensuring the venue continues to serve the region for decades to come.

The SCS will be owned and operated by Sunshine Coast Council (SCC), delivering a lasting legacy for the region through enhanced tourism, economic development, and increased opportunities for community engagement and active recreation.

I am reaching out to confirm if there was a detailed scope of work released to support development of Returnable Schedule 12 and Returnable Scheule 14?

I wanted to confirm the only Scope of Work information we were able to identify was Section 2.3.3 Scope, within document "GF26_292_GIICA-Expression_of_Interest-Sunshine_Coast_Stadium-Early_Works".

The scope includes the removal of existing structures within the proposed footprint of the main works, isolation of services, and removal of excess fill from site. The Early Works Contractor will be responsible for the planning, design, and delivery of deconstruction and demolition works, earthworks, and associated activities, including utility disconnections and site delineation.

This includes demolition of the existing western grandstand, plaza pavements and redundant services, partial site levelling, stockpiling of suitable material, and the removal of approximately 17,000 m³ of material from the eastern mound.

The Early Works Contractor will provide all labour, plant, materials, temporary works, supervision, permits, approvals, subcontractors and services necessary to deliver the Project in a safe, compliant, and coordinated manner.

Key activities include:

·
establishment of site access and security;

·
demolition;

·
site clearing and protection;

·
bulk earthworks;

·
utility management;

·
surface water management;

·
traffic management;

·
erosion and sediment controls;

·
environmental controls; and

·
technical reporting and documentation.

Could you please confirm?

GIICA confirms that the scope provided within the Expression of Interest Document is the only scope information that has currently been released.

A detailed scope document will be made available during the ITO Phase.

Thank you

Tenderers are responsible for determining and demonstrating compliance with all legislative licensing requirements.

title: REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL 19.26 CAR HIRE CONCESSION SERVICES: ONSLOW AIRPORT
description:
The Shire of Ashburton invites proposals from suitably qualified and experienced vehicle rental operators for the provision of car hire services at Onslow Airport.

The successful respondent(s) will be granted the right to operate a vehicle rental business from designated facilities within Onslow Airport under a Licence Agreement with the Shire of Ashburton.

Due to the limited availability of airport facilities and operational areas, the Shire intends to appoint no more than two (2) vehicle rental operators under this Request for Proposal. The Shire reserves the right to appoint one or two operators based on the outcome of the evaluation process and the best interests of the Shire.

The Shire is seeking a suitably experienced operator to provide vehicle rental services from Onslow Airport.

The successful respondent will have access to:

•	Dedicated car hire service counters within the terminal

•	Allocated vehicle parking areas

•	Branding opportunities within approved concession areas

•	Access to approximately 70,000 annual passenger movements

Respondents are encouraged to propose innovative service delivery models that best meet the needs of airport users.

title: T2026-023 Woorabinda Womens Sporting Hub - Netball Courts, Buildings Services and Associated Works
description:
Woorabinda Aboriginal Shire Council invites suitably qualified and experienced contractors for the delivery of Stage 2 of the Women’s Sporting Hub.

Stage 1 is the supply & installation of the modular clubhouse. (Works not within this tender)

Stage 2 comprises the establishment of the new Home of Women’s Sport in Woorabinda, featuring the construction of 2x multi-purpose sporting concrete courts, covered grandstand seating, concrete paths, design and installation of electrical, water, sewer and drainage to the clubhouse, playground and associated works as per the technical specification. The stage 2 scope along with the clubhouse will ensure the precinct provides the women of Woorabinda with a welcoming, family-friendly, safe community space.

Stage 3 works will follow, a time-frame TBC, comprising of a hardcover roof over the two courts with competition standard lighting.

As the 2nd stage of the Women’s Sporting Hub program, this package provides the key community infrastructure – 2 x courts, grandstand covered seating, fenced playground, concrete paths, building services and associated works that will contribute to a cohesive, high-quality sporting precinct for the Woorabinda community.

Works are to be completed in accordance with approved design documentation, applicable guidelines, and best-practice construction methods. Tender closing at 5.00 pm, Wednesday 9th September 2026.

publicQuestions.question:
Good morning,

In Part D – Schedule of Prices under “Termite Treatment”, it asks for confirmation that employee(s) hold a QBCC Termite Management – Chemical and a QBCC Termite Management – Physical licence. However, the services listed only require a QBCC Termite Management – Chemical licence.

Could you please confirm whether both licences are required, or only Chemical licensing for this tender?
publicQuestions.answer:
(edited on 13/Aug/2026 10:58 AM)

Thank you for your enquiry.

Tenderers are required to hold both a QBCC Termite Management – Chemical licence and a QBCC Termite Management – Physical licence.

While the termite treatment services currently listed in the Schedule of Rates primarily require a Termite Management – Chemical licence, the contract may include other termite management works that require a Termite Management – Physical licence. As subcontracting is not permitted under this arrangement, suppliers must be appropriately licensed to undertake the full range of potential termite-related services that may arise during the contract term.

Accordingly, the requirement for both licence types remains unchanged, and tenderers should ensure they can demonstrate compliance with both licensing requirements in their submission.

Please also note.

The QBCC Termite Management - Physical licence (along with the QBCC Termite Management – Chemical Licence) is only required if offering for the termite treatments, which is optional under this trade. The mandatory requirement for this SOA is the Pest Management Licence issued by Qld Health, which is required to undertake the basic and additional treatments etc.

publicQuestions.question:
Hi Procurement

Can you please confirm that if we have no subcontractors to propose for the services, we do not have to submit the Appendix C - Schedule of Subcontractors and that our submission will still be conforming ie not alternative?

Thanks
publicQuestions.answer: Yes Correct if you are not subcontracting you do not need to submit appendix C - Schedule of Subcontractors

publicQuestions.question:
Hi Procurement

Can you please confirm - if we are a pest control business, we are not allowed to provide subcontactors for termite works ONLY? but we are able to nominate for other pest services ie snakes, native species removal, etc?

Thank you
publicQuestions.answer:
Good morning,

Yes, that is correct. Termite works must be performed by the contracted business and cannot be subcontracted.

For any items outside the termite scope, subcontractors can be nominated in Appendix C and engaged subject to QBuild approval.

publicQuestions.question:
Hi Procurement

Can you confirm that the Annexure D Purchase Contract Conditions is for jobbing/ reactive services only? and that the contract for ongoing maintenance services will be created separately once the contractor is engaged under the SOA?
publicQuestions.answer:
Good morning,

This SOA covers reactive maintenance, planned maintenance, and housing vacant maintenance. A separate contract is required for ongoing regular servicing of certain sites, which is managed through our Service Maintenance team.

Could you please confirm whether the scope includes replacement, extension or upgrade of existing perimeter fencing, ball-stop fencing, player dugouts and spectator barriers, or whether the Contractor is only required to remove, modify and reinstate fencing impacted by the building works and associated access requirements.

Response

The contractor is only required to remove, modify and reinstate fencing impacted by the building works and associated access requirements.

publicQuestions.question:
RFI-01: Please confirm which edition of the AFL Preferred Community Facility Guidelines the AP-001 minimum sizes are drawn from (2019 or 2024). The two editions differ in several respects relevant to this design, including an additional Umpire Briefing Room requirement and the optional status of several rooms at Regional level in the 2024 edition.

RFI-02: Please confirm whether First Aid/Medical Room (15 sqm), Doctors Room (10 sqm) and Gym/Fitness Area (25 sqm) are to be treated as mandatory inclusions, given the current AFL guideline lists these as optional at Regional level.

RFI-03: Please confirm the public toilet provision (male, female and accessible sizing) tenderers should design to, as this is not included within AP-001.

RFI-04: Fig.3/DR-001 shows an indicative footprint of approximately 32m x 12m. Please confirm whether this is a fixed maximum building envelope or an indicative guide only, and whether tenderers may propose a larger footprint where necessary to meet AP-001 minimums.

RFI-05: Please confirm whether the amenity building must be a single connected structure, or whether a linked or separate two-pavilion arrangement (e.g. a detached change room block) would be acceptable on the site.

RFI-06: Please confirm whether a partial second storey/mezzanine, as referenced in Section 4.1 for the timekeeper/scoring box, is acceptable in principle, and advise any fire, access and structural requirements that would apply.

RFI-07: Please provide the site survey and geotechnical information referenced in the Contract Documents list, to allow tenderers to confirm building setout, levels and footing design.

RFI-08: Please confirm the minimum boundary setback/run-off distance applicable between the proposed building and the playing field boundary.

RFI-09: Please confirm the orientation requirement for the kiosk (Western side) - whether this is fixed relative to true north or relative to the oval/spectator side of the building.

RFI-10: Please confirm any specific corrosion/durability standards Council expects for coastal-environment cladding, fixings and external hardware, beyond general NCC compliance.

RFI-11: Please confirm whether operable/movable walls between change rooms, to allow flexible combined use, are a preference or a requirement.

RFI-12: Please clarify the expected timeframe and process for AFL design approval referenced in Section 4.2.1, and confirm whether this occurs prior to or following contract award.

RFI-13: Please advise whether existing utility service records (Telstra, Essential Energy) for the site are available

RFI-14: As the project is funded via a Commonwealth grant, please confirm whether there is a total project budget or cost cap tenderers should be designing to.

RFI-15: Please confirm the expected patronage/crowd size the facility should be sized for, relevant to the external covered viewing area, kiosk and public toilet sizing.
publicQuestions.answer:
The following responses are provided to clarify recent questions

RFI-01: Please confirm which edition of the AFL Preferred Community Facility Guidelines the AP-001 minimum sizes are drawn from (2019 or 2024). The two editions differ in several respects relevant to this design, including an additional Umpire Briefing Room requirement and the optional status of several rooms at regional level in the 2024 edition.

RESPONSE

The minimum sizes are drawn from the 2024 guidelines. Some building items have been excluded based on discussions with stake holders. The umpire briefing room is not required.

RFI-02: Please confirm whether First Aid/Medical Room (15 sqm), Doctors Room (10 sqm) and Gym/Fitness Area (25 sqm) are to be treated as mandatory inclusions, given the current AFL guideline lists these as optional at Regional level.

RESPONSE

Yes, these are mandatory items in the design

RFI-03: Please confirm the public toilet provision (male, female and accessible sizing) tenderers should design to, as this is not included within AP-001.

RESPONSE

Public toilets are not required in the new building only player amenities listed in the scope

RFI-04: Fig.3/DR-001 shows an indicative footprint of approximately 32m x 12m. Please confirm whether this is a fixed maximum building envelope or an indicative guide only, and whether tenderers may propose a larger footprint where necessary to meet AP-001 minimums.

RESPONSE

The building should be designed to the existing footprint; however, ramps/stairs can be accommodated outside of the footprint on the southwest side of the building. The transition to the field can be outside of this footprint but must be smooth. The Principal may, at its sole discretion, consider alternative tenders, provided the alternative tender meets the scope, functional intent and design concept expressed in the tender document. If an alternative tender is proposed, submit a detailed description of the alternative stating clearly the manner in which it differs from the detailed requirements of the RFT documents and including separate tender schedules applicable to the alternative.

Alternative tenders will not be considered unless the Tenderer has submitted a conforming tender.

RFI-05: Please confirm whether the amenity building must be a single connected structure, or whether a linked or separate two-pavilion arrangement (e.g. a detached change room block) would be acceptable on the site.

RESPONSE

Both options would be acceptable

RFI-06: Please confirm whether a partial second storey/mezzanine, as referenced in Section 4.1 for the timekeeper/scoring box, is acceptable in principle, and advise any fire, access and structural requirements that would apply.

RESPONSE

Partial second storey /mezzanine would be acceptable. Design requirements would have to be compliant with the NCC , however accessible access would not be required on the second floor.

RFI-07: Please provide the site survey and geotechnical information referenced in the Contract Documents list, to allow tenderers to confirm building setout, levels and footing design.

RESPONSE

The Site survey was provided in the original suit of documents , Ref S003-S-1, Geo Tec report was added 9 July Ref S-005H

RFI-08: Please confirm the minimum boundary setback/run-off distance applicable between the proposed building and the playing field boundary.

RESPONSE

Minimum Boundary run off is 4M to the player dugout/fences /gates. The building would need to accommodate these distances

RFI-09: Please confirm the orientation requirement for the kiosk (Western side) - whether this is fixed relative to true north or relative to the oval/spectator side of the building.

RESPONSE

The Kiosk is to be facing the oval/field of play

RFI-10: Please confirm any specific corrosion/durability standards Council expects for coastal-environment cladding, fixings and external hardware, beyond general NCC compliance.

RESPONSE

Nothing beyond general NCC requirements

RFI-11: Please confirm whether operable/movable walls between change rooms, to allow flexible combined use, are a preference or a requirement.

RESPONSE

Operable / movable walls are not a requirement but will be considered

RFI-12: Please clarify the expected timeframe and process for AFL design approval referenced in Section 4.2.1, and confirm whether this occurs prior to or following contract award.

RESPONSE

Concept design to be submitted with tender. Throughout the design process Council will be liaising with the AFL to ensure the building design meets the AFL minimal requirements

RFI-13: Please advise whether existing utility service records (Telstra, Essential Energy) for the site are available

RESPONSE

Not available

RFI-14: As the project is funded via a Commonwealth grant, please confirm whether there is a total project budget or cost cap tenderers should be designing to.

RESPONSE

Council will not be providing the project budget

RFI-15: Please confirm the expected patronage/crowd size the facility should be sized for, relevant to the external covered viewing area, kiosk and public toilet sizing.

RESPONSE

No public toilets required. Kiosk serving size to be a minimum of 30mtr Sq. No specific requirements for external covered viewing area

1.NCC lift requirement

Under NCC 2022, a two-storey Class 9b building is required to provide a means of access to the upper floor that complies with the accessibility provisions in NCC Section F. This typically requires a passenger lift or equivalent compliant access solution. This requirement was not contemplated in the original RFT scope and would represent a significant addition to the project cost and building footprint.

Please confirm whether council has considered this NCC requirement and whether a compliant accessible path of travel to the second floor is expected to be provided within the Contractor's scope. If so, please confirm whether a passenger lift is required or whether an alternative compliant access solution would be acceptable.

RESPONSE

Council has considered the accessibility requirements required for the second floor of the proposed building and is of the view that accessible access to the second floor is not required. This position is based on the anticipated limited patronage and use of the upper level and previous advice.

2. Floor-to-floor headroom

Based on the site levels available in S-005 and the current ground floor datum, a second floor FFL at 5RL to 5.5RL results in a floor-to-floor height that may not achieve a workable internal headroom at ground floor level. Please confirm the basis for the specified RL range, specifically whether it refers to the finished floor level of the second storey or another datum, and whether there is any flexibility in this specification to achieve a compliant and functional ground floor ceiling height.

RESPONSE

The specified RL range is based on the adjacent double storey building, with the intention that the proposed second storey floor level the new building aligns generally with the height and appearance of the existing building .There is an opportunity to excavate the current ground level to reach the acquired levels

3. Building footprint

The inclusion of a lift or equivalent accessible access solution, together with stair access, may require additional floor area within the 12m x 32m building footprint that was not allowed for in the original scope. Please confirm whether the footprint constraint remains fixed at 12m x 32m with these additional elements included, or whether any allowance for access infrastructure outside the primary footprint will be considered.

RESPONSE

The allowance for access infrastructure outside the primary footprint will be considered

RFI-

Please confirm whether a Development Application is genuinely not required given the development without consent classification stated in the RFT, or whether any conditions or notifications apply as a separate planning process (REF?)

RESPONSE

Council Can confirm no development application is required for this project

title: BSC 26/27 - T01 - St George Showground GAB Bore Construction
description:
Balonne Shire Council invites Tenders from suitably qualified Tenderers for the decommissioning of an existing bore (RN397) on Henry St, St George and construction of a new bore from the Gubberamunda Sandstone aquifer of the Great Artesian Basin (GAB) in St George Showground as described in more detail in Part 5 – Scope. 

Please put all queries and requests for information through the Vendor Panel forum portal. We request this to ensure everyone is receiving the same information at the same time.

title: TEN/2893 Waste Facilities Maintenance
description:
Council is inviting submissions from suitably qualified and experienced Suppliers for the provision of mechanical, hydraulic and associated maintenance services for Council's Waste Management and Resource Recovery Facilities.

The majority of works will be undertaken at the Bundaberg Materials Recovery Facility and Bundaberg Waste Management Facility located on University Drive, Bundaberg. The successful Supplier will also be required to provide maintenance, repairs and breakdown support across Council's landfill and transfer station network as required.

The Contract includes both scheduled preventative maintenance and reactive maintenance services. Key responsibilities will include the maintenance and repair of critical assets such as the MRF trommel, conveyor systems, balers, hydraulic equipment, motors, gearboxes, hydraulic tip wells, transfer station hydraulic gates and other operational plant and equipment. The Supplier may also be required to undertake inspections, fault diagnosis, ...

title: T2026-022 Woorabinda Gordon Henry Oval - Football Field, Buildings Services and Associated Works
description:
Woorabinda Aboriginal Shire Council invites suitably qualified and experienced contractors for the delivery of Stage 2 of the Gordon Henry Oval Facility.

Stage 1 is the supply & installation of the modular clubhouse. (Works not within this tender)

Stage 2 comprises the civil and landscape works to Field One, the supply and install of goal posts, scoreboard, coach and player seating, design and installation of electrical, water, sewer and drainage to the clubhouse and associated works as per the scope of works document.

Works are to be completed in accordance with approved design documentation, applicable guidelines, and best-practice construction methods. Tender closing at 5.00 pm, Wednesday 9th September 2026.

publicQuestions.question:
Good Afternoon

I note on the response schedult a requirement for a 250kl underground concrete tank. Is there a location this tank is to be and can I assume it must be trafficable top?
publicQuestions.answer:
Hi,

This has been changed to a 150,000L above ground solution in steel or poly.

It can be a single tank or multiple tanks. Please outline in your response.

It has to have (heavily) secure access points on top.

Please refer to "260819 Gordon Henry Oval Scope of Works - Field V2"

Thankyou.

publicQuestions.question:
Good Afternoon

We note in the documentation the requirement for a coach / players box. What number of people are needed to be seated in this as they vary in size requirements? There is also a requirement for an announcers box however we cannot find any specs for this. Can you elaborate more on this item?
publicQuestions.answer:
Hi,

The coaches boxes should be approx 4.8m long each.

The announcers box, similar to "Landmark K8110" The seating under would be for officials and separate from the players seating/coaches seating.

Thankyou

publicQuestions.question:

Can I please request some more detail on the electrical. Could you provide photos of existing ergon supply, main switchboard, field lighting controls and field light poles including estimated height. What size electrical supply is required to the new building?

publicQuestions.answer:

I would suggest a site inspection.

Please feel to make contact to organise.

Regards,

Michael Cahill

title: QPWS Fire Protective Clothing
description:
The Department of the Environment, Tourism, Science and Innovation invites Offers from Suppliers for Invitation to Offer (ITO) No. P253557 for the provision of Queensland Parks and Wildlife Services (QPWS) Fire Protective Clothing.

The scope of this ITO focusses on the supply of fire Personal Protective Clothing (PPC) across the State including jackets, trousers and shirts produced in accordance with Part B: Contract Details, Attachment 1 - QPWS Fire Protective Clothing Specifications for issue to fire trained staff and required to be worn by personnel when undertaking fire operations including planned burns and wildfire response.
buyer: Dept of the Environ, Tourism, Science and Innov
